sections.name: Brottö
sections.routeShape: linear gravel-road connector from Brottö brygga through Brottö skärgårdsjordbruk cultural reserve to the Ingmarsö gate
sourceHierarchyDraft: SAT official section page and step-by-step guide: route identity, public distance/difficulty/time, unmarked status, accessibility, route description and leave-no-trace advice.

SAT official PDF/GPX/KML/Outdooractive: current geometry artifact, start/end coordinates, computed distance and ascent/descent. Use official geometry but prefer SAT prose over Outdooractive surface metadata when they conflict.
Länsstyrelsen Stockholm: controlling source for Brottö kulturreservat rules, service absence and protected-area status.
Stockholms läns museum: cultural landscape, farming history, Highland cattle, stone walls, old farm/village context and map-based heritage layer.
Waxholmsbolaget/SL: primary public transport source. Static PDFs are useful only inside validity windows; live planning remains required for exact dates, request stops and summer timetable gaps.

Visit Roslagen, Ingmarsö local pages, Wikivoyage, Hiiker, AllTrails, Komoot, OSM/Wikimedia and blogs/forums: corroboration and conflict discovery only; not legal, route-distance or public-service authority.

routeGeometryDraft.ascentMeters: 15 m in SAT step guide; about 17 m in PDF/GPX extraction
geometrySourceNotes: SAT public page lists Brottö as Easy 1 km and says the trail starts at the ferry quay, follows the gravel road up through the farm/cultural landscape and ends at a gate toward Ingmarsö.

SAT step guide lists Easy 1 km, 20 minutes and 15 positive altitude meters; it says hikers disembark at the quay on Brottö's south coast, pass an information sign and small exhibition, walk about 100 m to an intersection, then continue another 850 m to the gate.
Official PDF en-s-a-t-brottoe-final.pdf is dated/updated 2024-07-01 and lists 1 km, 0:20 h, ascent 17 m, descent 13 m, easy, linear route, Outdooractive route 289598578.
Official GPX S A T Brottö Final has 37 trackpoints, Outdooractive metadata timestamp 2024-07-01T15:26:05.943Z and computes to about 0.961 km.
Official Google My Maps/KML route also computes to about 0.961 km and references Outdooractive route 289598578.
Iteration 2 OSM relation 19141225 check computed about 1.006 km, supporting the same rounded public 1 km value and refining route start/end pins.
No Brottö-specific route-change notice was found in iteration 1; unlike Ingmarsö, the official artifacts remain labelled Final from July 2024.
surfaceAndMarkingNotes: SAT says the section is entirely on gravel road and is not marked because it is straightforward; there are information/map signs at the beginning and end.

The PDF/Outdooractive artifact labels the surface as asphalt 1 km, but SAT prose, OSM/secondary sources and the cultural-landscape context support gravel/compacted farm road. Prefer SAT prose for user-facing surface.
AllTrails reports about 1.9 km out-and-back, apparently counting return to the quay. Do not use AllTrails as section-distance authority.
accessibilityNotes: SAT says Brottö is easy with stroller, limited mobility or wheelchair because the 1 km section is entirely on gravel road.
Länsstyrelsen information material says strollers/wheelchairs should use the road and the island is flat.
Treat as unusually accessible for SAT, with rural gravel, ferry, gate, farmyard and weather caveats rather than urban-grade accessibility.

sourceConflicts.summary: SAT and official PDF/GPX support about 1 km point-to-point; AllTrails reports about 1.9 km out-and-back.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use SAT/official GPX distance of 1.0 km and linear route shape. Keep AllTrails only as out-and-back secondary context.

sourceConflicts.summary: SAT prose says the route is on gravel road, while the official PDF/Outdooractive route data says asphalt 1 km.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use gravel road in app-facing descriptions because the official SAT prose, step guide and farm-road context are more appropriate for hikers than the platform surface classification.

sourceConflicts.summary: Secondary/nearby sources mention Ingmarsö services or a ferry waiting shelter, but Länsstyrelsen folder says Brottö itself has no toilet, waste bin or overnight possibility, and SAT points hikers to Ingmarsö/Svartsö for eating/sleeping.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Expose only Brottö brygga as transit and cultural information/heritage POIs. Keep Ingmarsö services as nearby/chaining context, not Brottö facilities.

sourceConflicts.summary: Generic outdoor platforms may suggest ordinary right-of-public-access camping, but Brottö is a cultural reserve and official material says no overnight possibility on Brottö, no camping/tent/lager site establishment and no damaging rock/soil/stone by fire.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Suppress camping, tent-place and fireplace claims on Brottö. Use conservative no-overnight/no-open-fire messaging and point overnight services to other islands.

sourceConflicts.summary: Brottö is sometimes discussed as nature/cultural landscape context, but the protected-area type is kulturreservat.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Label it as cultural reserve / kulturreservat rather than nature reserve.

sourceConflicts.summary: Earlier research used information, cultural_reserve and working_farm_landscape working labels, but the current draft has normalized them to schema-safe heritage POIs.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use the current normalized set: two on-route heritage POIs plus one optional off-route heritage detour. Do not treat the cultural interpretation points as TrailFacility service records.

sourceConflicts.summary: The cultural reserve, information sign, small exhibition and farmyard/grazing-landscape context overlap spatially and semantically around the quay-side visitor point.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use one app-facing heritage POI for Brottö skärgårdsjordbruk, with information sign, small exhibition, farmyard, Highland cattle, gate and private-land cautions in its description.

sourceConflicts.summary: Länsstyrelsen and Stockholms läns museum confirm Brottösand/Storsand brickworks and clay-pit remains west of Brottö brygga, but they are a detour away from the official 1 km SAT line.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Keep Brottösand/tegelbruk/lertag only as an optional off-route heritage detour with offRoute=true or routeProximity.status='off-route' during integration. Do not present it as on the SAT section or as a facility.

sourceConflicts.summary: Private cottage-rental listings may mention toilet, shower, grill or bathing near Brottö, and some secondary route pages merge Ingmarsö and Brottö services.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Suppress these as Brottö public trail facilities. Treat them as private lodging or Ingmarsö/general context only unless an official public facility source appears.

sections.descriptionDraft: Brottö is the shortest SAT section: a one-kilometer, easy gravel-road walk from Brottö brygga through a living small-scale archipelago farm landscape to the gate toward Ingmarsö. Present it as a cultural-reserve connector rather than a standalone service section: the walk is simple and unusually accessible, but it passes private working farm and grazing land with Highland cattle and has no confirmed toilet, water, food, waste or overnight facilities on Brottö itself.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Use Brottö brygga as the primary access point. Waxholmsbolaget table/line 13 lists Brottö (Ingmarsö) in the current spring/autumn 2026 PDF, valid 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026, updated 27 Mar 2026. The official summer 2026 static s13 PDF was not found in iterations 1-5; the s13 URL still resolved to a 2025 summer PDF with a 2025-06-03 last-modified header, so do not infer summer 2026 departures from it. Use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning for exact dates, holiday traffic, request stops, tickets and connecting buses; Waxholmsbolaget says connecting SL traffic is no longer included in line PDFs, so search the whole trip. Current line-13 symbols include B/b booking notes, X, |, a, p, z, G and period-limited H/I/V notes; check the exact departure legend rather than hardcoding service. Do not say normal SL tickets always cover Brottö/Ingmarsö; outside the Vaxholm-area SL-ticket zone and low-season period-ticket rules, Brottö normally needs a Waxholmsbolaget ticket for the outer part. Indirect access via Södra Ingmarsö, Norra Ingmarsö, Åsättra or Boda can be useful for chaining, but Brottö brygga is the direct SAT trailhead. Raise the pier semaphore when waiting for pickup; this complements, but does not replace, booking where B/b applies. Keep pier accessibility separate from trail accessibility: Visit Roslagen says Ingmarsö and Brottö piers are not accessibility-adapted, while SAT says the 1 km Brottö trail itself is unusually accessible.

accessMetadataDraft.name: Brottö brygga
accessMetadataDraft.description: Direct ferry access to the SAT Brottö trailhead on the south coast of Brottö. Waxholmsbolaget table 13 lists the stop as Brottö (Ingmarsö).

accessMetadataDraft.name: Brottö-Ingmarsö gate
accessMetadataDraft.description: End of the official Brottö GPX and transition toward Ingmarsö; useful for chaining Brottö with the Ingmarsö section and onward toward Finnhamn.

accessMetadataDraft.name: Södra Ingmarsö brygga
accessMetadataDraft.description: Indirect access via Ingmarsö services and the road/trail west to Brottö. Useful if the planner gives better departures, but not the primary Brottö trailhead.

accessMetadataDraft.name: Norra Ingmarsö brygga
accessMetadataDraft.description: Indirect access from Åsättra/Stockholm/Vaxholm via Norra Ingmarsö, useful for chaining but not direct to Brottö.

sections.campingRulesDraft: Do not expose camping, tent place, shelter or overnight on Brottö. Länsstyrelsen's Brottö information folder says there is no overnight possibility on Brottö, no toilet and no waste hut/bin; the reserve decision prohibits making land available for camping/caravan setup and establishing tent/lägerplats facilities. App wording should be: no campsite or overnight facility, and do not plan to overnight on Brottö. Suppress generic Komoot/AllTrails/right-of-public-access camping claims for this cultural reserve.
utilitiesDraft: No toilet, drinking water, waste, food, shop, campsite, shelter or overnight facility was confirmed on Brottö in iteration 1.
Brottö brygga has ferry access and likely a waiting shelter, but the waiting shelter is transit comfort only, not a hiking shelter or overnight/rest facility.
Nearest reliable services for food/water/toilet are on Ingmarsö, especially Södra Ingmarsö/guest harbor/Coop/krog/bakery, but these belong to the Ingmarsö section or nearby context.
The SAT section has information/map signs at the beginning and end and a small exhibition behind the quay-side sign.
waterSourcesDraft: No reliable drinking-water source was found on the Brottö section in iteration 1.
Use Ingmarsö service points for water planning when chaining Brottö with Ingmarsö; carry water if relying on Brottö alone.

facilitiesDraft.name: Brottö brygga
facilitiesDraft.description: Waxholmsbolaget ferry quay and direct SAT Brottö start point. Timetable details belong in access metadata; check live planning for exact date and request-stop details.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Brottö skärgårdsjordbruk kulturreservat
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Stockholm County's first cultural reserve, protecting a living small-scale archipelago farming landscape with old fields, meadows, stone walls, farm buildings and grazing Highland cattle. Pin at the quay-side information sign/small exhibition, which is the clearest visitor interpretation point; include farmyard/grazing, private-land, gate and cattle cautions here.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Södergärdet medieval field and stone wall
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Near-route heritage candidate: Länsstyrelsen describes older field-system and stone-wall remains near the road toward Ingmarsö, north of Södergärdet. Coordinate is approximate; present as low-key cultural landscape context, not a standalone attraction with infrastructure.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Brottösand and Storsand heritage detour
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Optional off-route westward detour from Brottö brygga along Storsandsvägen toward Brottösand/Storsand. Official sources document shore meadows, brickworks/clay-pit remains and a visitor nature/culture trail on existing roads and paths, but SAT itself continues east toward Ingmarsö. Do not treat as part of the main 1 km section geometry or as a facility.

notesDraft: Brottö is not marked with SAT ribbons/arrows because the route is straightforward; use information/map signs at the quay and end.
The section is unusually accessible for SAT because it follows a short gravel road, but still use rural-ferry/farm-road caveats.
Do not let trail accessibility imply end-to-end accessible travel: Visit Roslagen says Brottö and Ingmarsö piers are not accessibility-adapted.
Stay on the road/trail through the working farm landscape and respect private land, gates, grazing animals and farm operations.
Scottish Highland cattle graze large parts of the cultural reserve; keep distance and keep dogs leashed/controlled, especially March-September and around livestock.
No toilet, waste bin, drinking water, shop, food, campsite, shelter or overnight possibility was confirmed on Brottö itself.
Take waste back to the mainland or appropriate service points; do not rely on island waste handling.
No fireplace/firepit was confirmed; do not plan to light fires on Brottö, never light fires on rock and check current fire bans.

Brottösand/Storsand old brickworks, clay-pit remains, shore meadows and Storkärret/Sandvreten heritage exist west of Brottö brygga; iteration 4 promoted this to an explicit optional off-route heritage POI, not part of the official 1 km SAT line.
Brottö brygga waiting shelter is transit comfort only if retained; do not expose it as a hiking shelter.
Use live Waxholmsbolaget/SL planning for Brottö because request stops, holiday changes, ticket validity and summer timetable gaps matter.
Services on Södra Ingmarsö are useful nearby/chaining context, not Brottö section facilities.
facilitiesToSuppressDraft: Toilets on Brottö; Länsstyrelsen folder says no toilet.
Drinking water on Brottö; no reliable source confirmed any water point.
Waste bin/sopmaja on Brottö; Länsstyrelsen folder says none and SAT advises taking waste back where waste management works.
Any campsite, tent place, shelter, caravan setup or overnight pin on Brottö.
Any fireplace/firepit/grill on Brottö; use no-fire/conservative fire-ban wording.
Food, shop or restaurant as Brottö facilities; nearby Ingmarsö services belong to Ingmarsö context.
Private cottage-rental toilet, shower, grill or bathing claims as public Brottö trail facilities.
Brottö/Brottösand bathing-place claims as app-facing public swimming facilities; current Österåker and HaV bathing lists do not support them.
Brottö brygga waiting shelter as a hiking shelter or overnight facility.
Brottösand/tegelbruk/lertag as an on-route app POI or facility; iteration 4 keeps it only as an optional off-route heritage detour.
Naturkartan as a Brottö-specific citation until a useful specific page is found.
Komoot/AllTrails generic camping or route-distance claims as authoritative for this protected cultural-reserve section.

pendingFacilityDraft.reason: OSM/secondary sources show a ferry waiting shelter at Brottö brygga. Treat as transit comfort only; do not expose as TrailFacility shelter/overnight unless the app has transit-amenity metadata.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Brottö section research: official route facts and geometry, sparse on-section facilities, cultural-reserve rules/safety, access logistics and secondary-source conflict sweep.
keyFindings: SAT lists Brottö as Easy 1 km and the step guide says 20 minutes and 15 positive altitude meters. The official GPX/KML compute to about 0.961 km from Brottö brygga to the Ingmarsö gate.
Brottö is a deliberately unmarked section because it follows a straightforward gravel road from the south-coast ferry quay, through the farm/cultural landscape, to a gate toward Ingmarsö.
Official PDF/Outdooractive labels the surface as asphalt, but SAT prose and local context support gravel/compacted farm road. Use gravel road in app-facing text.
SAT says the whole 1 km section is suitable for stroller, limited mobility or wheelchair; retain rural gravel-road, ferry, gate and farm-context caveats.
Brottö brygga is the primary direct access and should be the only normal app-facing facility for iteration 1, typed as transit. It is served by Waxholmsbolaget table/line 13 as Brottö (Ingmarsö).
Current line 13 PDF is valid 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026; no current 2026 summer s13 static PDF was found. Use live planning for summer, holidays, request stops, tickets and connections.

Brottö should be modeled as Brottö skärgårdsjordbruk kulturreservat, Stockholm County's first cultural reserve, with working small-scale farming, Highland cattle, stone walls, farm buildings, meadows and historical landscape values.
Länsstyrelsen material says there is no toilet, no waste hut/bin and no overnight possibility on Brottö. Suppress toilet, water, waste, camping, shelter, shop, food and fire facilities.
Brottö brygga has an information sign/QR and small exhibition nearby, and the section end has another information/map sign. These are POI/information context, not service facilities.
Generic camping/right-of-public-access claims from secondary platforms conflict with Brottö cultural-reserve guidance and should be suppressed.
Brottösand/old brickworks/clay-pit heritage is real but not yet pinned well enough or verified as on-route; keep pending/off-route context for later iterations.
Nearby Ingmarsö services are useful for planning a chain hike but should not be duplicated as Brottö facilities.
remainingQuestionsForNextIterations: Run a precise coordinate pass for the Brottö quay information sign, end/gate sign, waiting shelter and any small exhibition point.
Pin Brottösand/tegelbruk/lertag and decide whether it is a useful off-route heritage POI or should remain suppressed.
Recheck whether any newer Länsstyrelsen management-plan or service page changes the visitor-facing rules; current public page, folder and 2004 decision already support conservative treatment.
Recheck Waxholmsbolaget/SL for current 2026 summer table 13 and request-stop/ticket details.
Confirm in later iterations whether the ferry waiting shelter should remain pending transit metadata rather than a facility.
Check Naturkartan and other municipal/outdoor guide layers again, but do not use them unless a Brottö-specific page appears.
Validate final schema types for POIs because cultural_reserve, information and working_farm_landscape may need normalization during app integration.

keyFindings: The 2014 Länsstyrelsen skötselplan PDF was located. It is dated 2014-11-17 and replaces earlier management plans, not the 2004 reserve-formation decision or visitor rules. It does not add toilets, water, waste, camping, shelter or overnight services.

Brottö remains a no-service hiking section. A dedicated falsification pass found no official/current support for public toilet, drinking water, waste, food/shop, campsite, fireplace, bathing place, hiker shelter or public service on Brottö itself.

Decide whether the end/gate information sign should be a separate POI or remain route/access metadata only.
Keep watching for any official/local public-service claims, but current evidence strongly supports no Brottö services.

iterationSummaries.focus: Final Brottö closure: access/ticket timetable verification, no-service falsification, heritage/coordinate QA, route geometry check and integration risk review.
keyFindings: No confirmed Brottö service additions were found in the final pass. Keep only Brottö brygga as transit/ferry access and keep visitor interpretation as heritage/context, not service facilities.

Waxholmsbolaget v13 is current for 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026, updated 27 Mar 2026. The s13 URL still served a 2025 summer PDF when checked on 2026-04-26, so summer 2026 must be planned live.

Ticket wording must stay cautious: all SL tickets apply year-round only in the defined Vaxholm-area zone, while Brottö normally needs Waxholmsbolaget ticket handling for the outer-archipelago part unless low-season period-ticket rules apply.

routeGeometryDraft.estimatedTime: 4.5 hours in SAT step guide; 5:00 h in PDF/Outdooractive
geometrySourceNotes: SAT lists Svartsö as Easy 17.9 km and describes nearly eighteen kilometers mostly on gravel roads through open pasture landscapes.
SAT step guide lists Easy 17.9 km, 4.5 hours and 79 m elevation gain; it describes two loops connected by gravel road, with several ferry quays enabling shorter linear or out-and-back variants.
Official PDF en-sat-svartsoe-final.pdf is dated/updated 2024-10-26 and lists 17.9 km, 5:00 h, 79 m ascent, 72 m descent, moderate difficulty, Outdooractive route 259162059.
Official GPX has 652 trackpoints and computes to about 17.919 km; official Google My Maps/KML computes to about 17.903 km.

OSM relation 19014515 is tagged SAT Etapp Svartsö, length 17.9 km, direction anticlockwise and network rwn, but a naive unique-way sum can undercount because the official figure-eight/shared connector topology repeats walking.
surfaceAndMarkingNotes: Use 'mostly gravel/compacted roads with local forest/path sections' as app-facing surface wording.
SAT prose emphasizes mostly gravel roads and OSM member surfaces skew gravel/compacted; PDF/Outdooractive classifies 10.3 km asphalt, 3.7 km forested/wild trail, 2.6 km path and 1.3 km unknown.
SAT marking exists in recommended direction on the main route, but two local trail parts are flower-marked rather than SAT-marked.

Western local trail is best described as locally white-wood-anemone-marked because the SAT trail marking section and step guide support this; keep a source-conflict note that FAQ-style text has also referenced sunflowers. Eastern local trail is bluebell-marked, with an about 800 m non-SAT-marked stretch due to landowner restrictions.
accessibilityNotes: SAT says almost all Svartsö sections are suitable for stroller, wheelchair or limited mobility, with exceptions on the western south path and the eastern loop north of Söderboudd.
Do not infer full-journey accessibility from trail accessibility. Ferry piers, vessels, boarding weather and Norra Svartsö winter/ice service caveats can affect access.

sections.descriptionDraft: Svartsö is a long but easy SAT island section: a roughly 17.9 km figure-eight of gravel/compacted roads and local forest/path sections through open grazing landscapes, lakes, villages and several ferry-access spurs. It can be started from Norra Svartsö, Alsvik, Skälvik or Söderboudd, so present it as a multi-access loop network rather than a single-start trail. Alsvik is the main service cluster, with seasonal public toilet/water at the guest harbour and food/shop options nearby; Norra Svartsö adds a private-hosted off-season toilet/water fallback at the hotel. Many other amenities are seasonal, paid, customer-only or private.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Svartsö can be reached via four SAT-relevant Waxholmsbolaget piers: Norra Svartsö, Alsvik, Skälvik and Söderboudd. In current spring/autumn 2026 material, Norra Svartsö is primarily line 10A/10B with some 13B variants, while Alsvik, Skälvik and Söderboudd are line 13A/13B stops; Skälvik is about a 700 m spur from the SAT east-west road. Rechecked 2026-04-26: v10/v13 PDFs are current for 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026. The line timetable service does not yet expose summer 2026 line 10/13 tables; direct s10/s13 PDFs still resolve to summer 2025, so use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning for 19 Jun-16 Aug 2026 and exact dates. Booking/request-stop symbols such as B/b/C/c/X/|/a/p/z plus period/goods symbols can matter depending on line/departure; check the exact departure legend. Do not say ordinary SL tickets always cover Svartsö: year-round ordinary SL validity applies only in the inner Stockholm-Vaxholm/Rindö area, while Svartsö normally needs a Waxholmsbolaget ticket for the outer part unless low-season period-ticket rules apply. Raise the pier semaphore where required; plan the whole trip in SL/Waxholmsbolaget because connecting bus traffic is no longer reliably embedded in line PDFs.

accessMetadataDraft.description: Eastern access point for linear hikes or exits after the eastern loop. SAT says the four-way intersection to Söderboudd is 3.3 km along gravel road; served by line 13A/13B variants depending on timetable period and direction.

sections.accessibilityDraft: The SAT Svartsö route is mostly easy road walking and many sections are described as suitable for stroller, wheelchair or limited mobility, but exclude the western south path and the eastern loop north of Söderboudd from that broad accessibility claim. Do not mark the full journey as guaranteed accessible: ferry piers, boarding, weather, local trail/path sections and winter ice access can vary.
sections.campingRulesDraft: Do not expose a campsite on Svartsö. SAT FAQ says there are no campsites on Svartsö. Local Hembygdsgården tenting references are informal/local allemansrätten context only, not a recommendation, rest area or mappable site. Avoid homes, private land, fields, crops and active pasture; keep dogs controlled and respect livestock.
utilitiesDraft: Confirmed seasonal public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour; SAT says it is not available in winter.
Confirmed seasonal public water at Alsvik guest harbour; do not expose lakes as drinking-water taps.

Private-hosted/year-round toilet and water fallback at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell near Norra Svartsö is supported by SAT winter/off-season guidance; verify before relying and do not treat hotel showers/guest amenities as public.
Svartsö Lanthandel, café, Svartsö Krog and Bistro Sågen are confirmed food/shop/service candidates, but opening hours vary by season and customer/booking caveats apply.
No official campsite or public hiker shelter confirmed.
No official public fireplace/firepit confirmed; one grill candidate near Sågens brygga remains pending/suppressed until stronger source confirms public use.
Waste should default to pack-out guidance. Svartsö ÅVC and harbor waste/miljöstation references are not normal trail-litter bins and need caveats.
The four ferry-quay transit pins duplicate access metadata. During integration, render ferry stops from access metadata or use transit facilities as fallback, not both.
waterSourcesDraft: Use Alsvik guest harbour as the strongest confirmed public water refill point, seasonal and not in winter.
Svartsö Skärgårdshotell near Norra Svartsö is a private-hosted/year-round water fallback per SAT winter/off-season guidance; verify before relying.
Do not expose Storträsket, Lillträsket or other lakes as drinking water. SAT describes Storträsket as the island drinking-water source, not a public tap.
Restaurants/shop may provide water or toilets for guests/customers, but do not model those as unconditional public refill points without confirmation.

facilitiesDraft.name: Public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Not in winter per SAT
facilitiesDraft.description: Public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour, the main service cluster for the Svartsö section. Seasonal: SAT says no toilet/water here in winter.

facilitiesDraft.name: Water at Alsvik guest harbour
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Not in winter per SAT
facilitiesDraft.description: Confirmed public water refill point at Alsvik guest harbour, seasonal and not island-wide tap coverage.

facilitiesDraft.name: Svartsö Lanthandel

facilitiesDraft.name: Svartsö bryggcafé / café at Lanthandeln
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Likely seasonal/variable opening
facilitiesDraft.description: Café service in the Alsvik/Lanthandel cluster. Treat as opening-hours dependent.

facilitiesDraft.name: Svartsö Krog
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal/variable opening; current published pattern is mainly April-October with strongest daily coverage in July-mid August.
facilitiesDraft.description: Restaurant east of Alsvik on or near the route. Confirm current opening hours and booking before relying on it.

facilitiesDraft.name: Bistro Sågen
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal/variable opening; current 2026 pattern is spring weekends, summer peak service and reduced late-season opening into September.
facilitiesDraft.description: Restaurant near the central/southern SAT route. SAT step guide says it is 500-600 m south of the four-way intersection and worth visiting; verify opening hours and booking before relying on it.

facilitiesDraft.name: Alsvik / Hembygdsgården bathing area
facilitiesDraft.description: Alsvik/Hembygdsgården bathing cluster. Naturkartan lists two very nearby Svartsö bathing entries, and local/Värmdö island material says bathing is available by Hembygdsgården. Treat as one swimming facility unless later map work proves separate maintained spots; no official HaV sampled-water-quality status found.

facilitiesDraft.name: Svartsö Skärgårdshotell year-round toilet
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Reported year-round in SAT winter/off-season guidance, but private-hosted; verify before relying.
facilitiesDraft.access: Private-hosted/off-season fallback; reported year-round on the southeast side of the main building, middle door. Verify before relying.
facilitiesDraft.description: Year-round toilet fallback near Norra Svartsö from SAT winter/off-season guidance. Treat as private-hosted and verify-before-relying, not a municipal public toilet.

facilitiesDraft.name: Water at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Reported year-round in SAT winter/off-season guidance, but private-hosted; verify before relying.
facilitiesDraft.access: Private-hosted/off-season fallback; SAT says water is available year-round at the middle door on the southeast side of the main building. Verify before relying.
facilitiesDraft.description: Year-round water fallback near Norra Svartsö from SAT winter/off-season guidance. Use as a caveated fallback, not as an unconditional public tap.

facilitiesDraft.name: Norra Svartsö ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Northern ferry access point and one valid start for the Svartsö SAT network. Winter service can be limited when ice is not broken on the north side.

facilitiesDraft.name: Alsvik/Ahlsvik ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Most service-rich ferry access point, by shop/café/guest harbour. Served by Waxholmsbolaget line 13; local page says Waxholmsbolaget serves it year-round and Cinderella seasonally.

facilitiesDraft.name: Skälvik ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Southern ferry access point. SAT says hikers arriving at Skälvik follow gravel road north about 700 m to rejoin the route.

facilitiesDraft.name: Söderboudd ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Eastern/southern ferry access point. Useful for shorter linear variants or exits after the east loop.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Storträsket and Boholmen
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Svartsö's largest lake and a scenic heritage/nature context. SAT describes Storträsket as the island's drinking-water source, and local/Värmdö sources say residents around the lakes take drinking water from them; this is not a public water refill point. Boholmen in Storträsket is linked to stories from the 1719 Russian ravages, when islanders hid there with their possessions.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Svartsö Hembygdsgården / former mission house
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Former mission house near Alsvik, inaugurated in 1880 and now used as Svartsö's community/heritage building. Local sources mention tenting by Hembygdsgården under allemansrätten, but there is no organized campsite on the island, so do not map it as a campsite or rest area.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Stenhuset in Alsvik
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Privately owned stone manor/heritage house in Alsvik, built in 1732 and identified by RAÄ as having high cultural-historical value. Present as view-from-road heritage context only; do not imply public courtyard or interior access.
pointsOfInterestDraft.warning: Private property; view respectfully from public road/path only.

Ferry waiting shelters at quays, if later mapped, are transit comfort only and not hiker shelters.
Render ferry stops from accessMetadataDraft as the primary access layer; keep transit facilities only as fallback if the app cannot consume access metadata. Never render both layers at once.

Close gates, stay on roads/marked paths through pasture and respect private houses, fields and crops.
Do not expose lakes as potable water. Storträsket is described as an island drinking-water source, not a public tap.
Treat Alsvik/Hembygdsgården as one bathing cluster with Naturkartan source aliases and no official HaV sampled-water-quality status unless later verified.
Keep Lillträsket and route-wide grazing landscape context in description/notes rather than precise map pins unless later integration supports scenic micro-POIs or route-wide context markers.
Keep defibrillators as guarded emergency metadata, not attraction POIs or ordinary trail facilities.
Use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning because request stops, booking symbols, summer timetable updates and ticket validity matter.

Ferry waiting shelters as hiking shelters or overnight facilities.

Nearby island services from Ingmarsö, Brottö, Finnhamn or Möja.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Svartsö research: official route facts and geometry, multi-pier access, Alsvik service cluster, nature/culture POIs, rules/safety and broad source-conflict sweep.
keyFindings: SAT lists Svartsö as Easy 17.9 km and the step guide says 4.5 hours and 79 m gain; the official PDF/Outdooractive artifact says moderate and 5:00 h. Prefer SAT page/step guide for difficulty and carry the PDF conflict forward.

Official GPX/KML compute to about 17.9 km and support the public distance. The route should be modeled as a multi-access figure-eight/loop network with valid starts at Norra Svartsö, Alsvik, Skälvik and Söderboudd.
Svartsö is mostly gravel/road walking with local path sections. Some local paths are flower-marked rather than SAT-marked; exact western flower icon naming needs later verification.
Alsvik is the primary hiker service cluster. SAT confirms public toilet and water at Alsvik guest harbour, but not in winter.
Svartsö Lanthandel, the café/bryggcafé, Svartsö Krog and Bistro Sågen are confirmed food/service candidates, all with opening-hours, seasonality or customer/booking caveats.
No organized campsite was confirmed. SAT FAQ says no campsites on Svartsö; Hembygdsgården tenting references should remain allemansrätten/private-land context only.

No official public trail shelter or official maintained fireplace/firepit was confirmed in iteration 1. Ferry waiting shelters are transit comfort only; a Sågens brygga grill candidate remains pending.
Naturkartan/Värmdö support Ahlsvik/Svartsö bathing places, but HaV monitoring was not found for Svartsö/Ahlsvik. Use swimming POI(s) without official sampled-water-quality claims.
Storträsket, Lillträsket, Boholmen, Hembygdsgården, Stenhuset and the open grazing landscape are useful nature/heritage contexts. Do not expose Storträsket or lakes as drinking-water taps.
Access should rely on live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning. v10/v13 static PDFs are current for spring/autumn 2026, while s10/s13 summer PDFs still showed 2025 in iteration 1.
Ticket wording must not say ordinary SL tickets cover Svartsö generally; Svartsö is beyond the Vaxholm-area SL ticket zone and Waxholmsbolaget ticket/low-season period-ticket rules matter.
Private/paid services such as hotel, glamping, sjöbodar, sauna, showers and restaurant toilets should not be rendered as free public hiker facilities.
remainingQuestionsForNextIterations: Verify exact coordinates for Badplats Svartsö and whether Naturkartan's nearby toilet is public, seasonal and distinct from Alsvik guest harbour.
Verify Sågens brygga grill/fireplace with stronger official/local source or suppress it.
Check Värmdö/guest-harbour waste and ÅVC treatment: decide whether any waste facility belongs in app data or only notes.
Recheck current 2026 summer s10/s13 timetable PDFs in later iterations.
Verify western local trail flower marking name and local path/surface details.
Check whether any public defibrillator/first-aid facility should be captured, especially Skärgårdshotellet/off-season SAT note.
Clarify if Norra Svartsö/Svartsö Skärgårdshotell year-round toilet/water should be a public facility, customer/guest facility or only off-season services note.
Resolve whether Hembygdsgården tenting reference should remain suppress-only or a rule note.
Check whether Stenhuset should remain a POI or be folded into Alsvik heritage context due to private-property sensitivity.

iterationSummaries.focus: Targeted Svartsö validation: bathing coordinates, fire/waste decisions, Norra Svartsö off-season services, local marking/surface conflicts and schema/integration QA.
keyFindings: Bathing should be modeled as one Alsvik/Hembygdsgården cluster, not two separate Naturkartan facilities. Use [59.438753, 18.654693] as the strongest beach-center coordinate and retain Naturkartan Badplats Ahlsvik Svartsö / Badplats Svartsö as aliases.
HaV registered Värmdö bathing-water list still did not show Svartsö/Ahlsvik. Do not show official sampled-water-quality status.
Femsundviken is an Ingmarsö bathing place and should be suppressed for sat-svartso as secondary-source bleed.

No public fireplace/firepit should be promoted. Sågens brygga remains pending or suppressed because only OSM/grillplats-style sources support it, and Bistro Sågen material describes a private/customer guest dock rather than a confirmed public hiker firepit.

Svartsö ÅVC and Alsvik guest-harbor miljöstation should remain conditional/pending metadata, not normal trail waste facilities. Primary app guidance should remain pack out trash, using public harbor waste only if necessary.

SAT off-season guidance supports year-round toilet, water and defibrillator at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell near Norra Svartsö. Add toilet/water only as private-hosted verify-before-relying fallback; keep the defibrillator as emergency metadata/POI if no app type exists.
Do not expose hotel showers, guest kitchen, paid lodging, hostel rooms, sauna or glamping as public hiker facilities.

Marking conflict was narrowed: western local trail should be described as white-wood-anemone-marked, with a retained conflict note for sunflower wording; eastern local trail is bluebell-marked and includes an about 800 m non-SAT-marked stretch due to landowner restrictions.

Surface wording should be mostly gravel/compacted roads with local forest/path sections. Keep the PDF/Outdooractive asphalt classification as a conflict, but do not use it as app-facing surface unless later evidence supports it.

Add explicit accessibility wording: many route sections are suitable for stroller/wheelchair/limited mobility, but the western south path, eastern loop north of Söderboudd, ferry piers, boarding, weather and winter ice access are caveats.
Demote route-wide open grazing landscape from a precise mapped POI to section narrative/rule context unless integration later supports route-wide context markers.
Ferry quays appear both as access metadata and transit facilities. Integration should render one layer or the other, not duplicate pins.
remainingQuestionsForNextIterations: Verify whether the Svartsö Skärgårdshotell toilet/water should remain public-facing facilities or move to an off-season services note after checking current hotel wording/contact details.
Run one more broad services pass for defibrillator/emergency metadata and whether the app can represent it cleanly.
Recheck summer 2026 s10/s13 timetable PDFs and access symbol details.
Keep looking for official/local confirmation of any public firepit; otherwise suppress Sågens brygga grill in iteration 3 or 4.
Check whether the Alsvik/Hembygdsgården bathing cluster has a distinct public toilet independent of Alsvik guest harbour.
Decide whether Stenhuset stays as its own heritage POI or folds into Alsvik heritage context.

iterationSummaries.focus: Svartsö cleanup/falsification pass: current access PDFs and tickets, service caveats, emergency metadata, POI pruning, pending fire/waste/beach decisions and integration QA.
keyFindings: Access metadata remains correct. Rechecked on 2026-04-26: v10 and v13 are current for 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026, while s10 and s13 still served 2025 summer PDFs. Summer 2026 should remain live-planner-only.
Line mapping remains Alsvik/Skälvik/Söderboudd on line 13 and Norra Svartsö primarily on line 10, with some line 13B appearances. Keep Norra Svartsö winter/ice caveat.
Booking/request symbols B, b, C/c, X, |, a, p and z remain relevant depending on line/departure; ticket wording should continue to say Svartsö is beyond the Vaxholm-area SL ticket zone.

Alsvik guest harbour toilet/water are the strongest public hiker utilities and are seasonal/not winter. Svartsö Skärgårdshotell toilet/water can remain as private-hosted year-round fallback, with verify-before-relying caveats.
Customer-only or paid amenities remain suppressed: lanthandel paid/when-open toilet, restaurant/café toilets, hotel/hostel room toilets/showers, guest kitchen, sauna and guest-harbour shower.

Two defibrillators were identified by SAT winter 2026 guidance: one at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell and one by the lanthandel entrance. Move these out of pointsOfInterestDraft and keep them as guarded emergency metadata, not attractions or normal facilities.
Keep Hembygdsgården as a heritage POI, but do not turn its tenting reference into a campsite, rest area or recommendation.
Keep Storträsket/Boholmen as the main lake/heritage POI. Fold Lillträsket into lake-corridor narrative unless later integration wants scenic micro-POIs.
Keep Stenhuset as a view-from-road heritage POI with a strong private-property warning.
Fold route-wide grazing/open landscape into description/rule notes rather than a precise map pin.
Keep Hjälmö-Lådna pending/off-route only, marked notTrailFacility/offRoute, because it is a real nearby nature reserve but not part of sat-svartso geometry.

Do not promote Sågens brygga grill/fireplace. OSM has a barbecue node, but no SAT/Värmdö/Naturkartan/local-owner confirmation of public hiker use was found and Bistro Sågen frames the brygga as customer-adjacent.
Alsvik guest-harbor miljöstation and Svartsö ÅVC stay guarded pending metadata, not normal trail waste facilities. SAT guidance remains pack out trash, using public harbor waste only if necessary.
Suppress the second unnamed south beach as a swimming facility; only OSM maps a natural beach and no official/local bathing-place source was found.
Integration should prefer accessMetadataDraft for ferry rendering and use transit facilities only as fallback, avoiding duplicate ferry pins.
remainingQuestionsForNextIterations: One more pass should decide whether the private-hosted Skärgårdshotell toilet/water stays in facilitiesDraft or moves to a winter/off-season services note.
Confirm whether emergency metadata should remain pending or move to a future app-specific emergency/AED structure.
Recheck summer 2026 s10/s13 PDFs in iteration 4/5.
If no stronger firepit source appears, suppress Sågens brygga grill entirely by iteration 5.
Final schema pass should decide whether transit ferry pins remain in facilitiesDraft or only in accessMetadataDraft.

iterationSummaries.focus: Svartsö final-shape pass before closure: access-layer model, private/off-season services, pending suppressions, POI descriptions and JSON/schema QA.
keyFindings: Access metadata should be the primary ferry layer. Norra Svartsö is primarily line 10A/10B with some 13B variants, while Alsvik, Skälvik and Söderboudd are line 13A/13B stops. Transit facilities remain only as fallback to avoid duplicate ferry pins.
The 2026-04-26 timetable state remains unchanged: v10/v13 are current spring/autumn 2026 PDFs and s10/s13 still show 2025 summer PDFs. Live planning is still required for summer 2026.

Alsvik guest-harbor toilet/water remain the primary public utilities and should be marked not-in-winter. Svartsö Skärgårdshotell toilet/water stay in facilitiesDraft only as private-hosted year-round fallback with verify-before-relying wording.
Svartsö Lanthandel should remain a food/shop service only; do not promote its paid/when-open customer toilet as a public toilet.

Sågens brygga grill should be suppressed as a public fireplace. Keep only as a pending, notTrailFacility, needs-owner-verification candidate because OSM/grillplats evidence is not enough and Bistro Sågen describes a customer-adjacent guest dock.

Alsvik harbor miljöstation and Svartsö ÅVC remain guarded waste metadata, not normal trail litter facilities. App guidance should continue to default to pack-out trash and use harbor waste only if necessary.
The unnamed south beach remains suppressed as a swimming facility; only OSM supports it as a natural beach. The app-facing swimming facility should remain the Alsvik/Hembygdsgården cluster.
Hjälmö-Lådna is real nearby protected-area context but off-route for this section; keep only as off-route metadata if the app supports that layer.
Move the two defibrillators out of pending facilities into emergencyMetadataDraft so they are not accidentally rendered as attractions, POIs or normal trail facilities.
Keep Storträsket/Boholmen, Hembygdsgården and Stenhuset as the three app-facing heritage/nature POIs. Lillträsket and grazing landscapes belong in narrative/rule notes rather than precise pins.
No organized campsite exists on Svartsö. Hembygdsgården tenting references are allemansrätten context only and should not become a campsite, rest area or recommendation.
remainingQuestionsForNextIterations: Final pass should recheck whether s10/s13 summer 2026 PDFs have appeared after the current 2025 static PDFs.
Final pass should decide whether transit fallback facilities remain in the contribution or should be removed after app integration supports accessMetadataDraft.
Final pass should verify no pending notTrailFacility item still has a renderable TrailFacility type.
Final pass should sanity-check emergencyMetadataDraft field naming against later app schema before integration.

iterationSummaries.focus: Svartsö closure pass: final access/timetable verification, facilities/services closure, pending suppression QA, POI/rules wording and JSON/schema readiness.
keyFindings: Final access model is safe: render ferry access from accessMetadataDraft as primary, with the four transit facilities retained only as fallback. Integration must never render both layers at once.

Rechecked 2026-04-26: v10 and v13 PDFs remain current for 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026. Summer 2026 line 10/13 static tables are still not exposed; direct s10/s13 PDFs still resolve to summer 2025, so use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning for 19 Jun-16 Aug 2026.
Line mapping remains Norra Svartsö primarily line/table 10A/10B with some 13B variants, and Alsvik, Skälvik and Söderboudd on line/table 13A/13B. Skälvik remains a 700 m spur from the SAT route.

Ticket wording should remain cautious: year-round ordinary SL validity applies only in the inner Stockholm-Vaxholm/Rindö area; Svartsö normally needs a Waxholmsbolaget ticket for the outer part unless low-season period-ticket rules apply.

No missing high-confidence exposed facility was found. Keep Alsvik guest-harbor toilet/water as seasonal public utilities and mark not-in-winter; keep Svartsö Skärgårdshotell toilet/water only as private-hosted, verify-before-relying year-round fallback.

Keep Svartsö Lanthandel, Svartsö bryggcafé, Svartsö Krog and Bistro Sågen as food/service facilities with opening-hours, booking, customer and seasonality caveats. Do not expose Lanthandel's paid/inside-store toilet as a normal public toilet.

Do not add campsite, fireplace/firepit or hiking shelter. SAT and local checks still do not support an organized campsite or public trail firepit on Svartsö; ferry waiting shelters are ferry-access comfort only.

Pending/suppressed candidates are safe against normal rendering: Sågens brygga grill, harbor miljöstation, Svartsö ÅVC, the unnamed south beach and Hjälmö-Lådna all remain notTrailFacility/off-route/conditional metadata. Future importers should ignore pendingFacilityDraft unless explicitly reviewed and never render notTrailFacility entries.

Keep defibrillators in emergencyMetadataDraft, outside facilitiesDraft and pointsOfInterestDraft. The field is schema-extension metadata and should not render as an attraction, POI or ordinary TrailFacility.

Final POI model is three app-facing heritage/nature POIs: Storträsket/Boholmen, Hembygdsgården and Stenhuset. Lillträsket, grazing landscape, dog/gate/private-land rules and camping remain narrative/rule notes.
Keep Alsvik/Hembygdsgården as the only exposed swimming cluster. Naturkartan/local sources support it; no HaV sampled-water-quality status was found.
Final JSON QA found no blocking issues: Svartsö draft arrays have no duplicate IDs, exposed facility/POI types are valid, and pending entries have no renderable type.

geometrySourceNotes: SAT lists Möja as Easy 13.8 km. The step guide says 4:30 hours walking time, 85 m elevation gain, and states the section is one of the SAT sections that does not form a complete loop.
Official PDF en-sat-moeja-new.pdf is updated 2025-06-05 and lists 13.8 km, 4:30 h, 83 m ascent, 79 m descent and moderate difficulty.
Outdooractive route 317486871 lists 13.8 km, 4:30 h, 83 m ascent, 79 m descent, highest point 29 m and lowest point 1 m.
Iteration 2 downloaded both the official Google Drive GPX and Outdooractive GPX and computed 13.797 km from 534 trackpoints.
Iteration 3 rechecked both GPX sources; both remain accessible and compute to 13.797 km from 534 trackpoints.

Official Google My Maps export is accessible as KML/KMZ. The force-KML URL returns one rounded LineString with 232 coordinate points and computes to about 13.778 km; use GPX as canonical because it is denser.
Outdooractive page exposes GPX/KML/FIT buttons, but unauthenticated direct export only succeeded for GPX during iteration 3; KML redirected or was blocked and FIT returned 403.

Iteration 4 rechecked official SAT, PDF, Google Drive GPX, Outdooractive GPX, Google My Maps KML/KMZ, OSM relation 19023630, Wikidata and major secondary trail pages. No richer official geometry was found; official GPX remains canonical.

OSM relation 19023630 now tags distance=13.8 km, but measured member geometry is about 9.798 km and appears to omit the Hamn-to-Berg return. Wikidata Q133724252 still reports 10.4 km and should be treated as stale/noncanonical.
surfaceAndMarkingNotes: Use 'almost entirely gravel/local road walking' for app-facing surface wording.
SAT says the trail is easy to follow because it runs along a gravel road; the PDF/Outdooractive track-type layer says roughly 13.4 km road and 0.4 km dirt road.
Do not imply a forest trail for the SAT main route. Möja-Björndalen/naturstigen is a nearby/local optional nature trail and should not be merged into SAT geometry until explicitly verified.
SAT markings are blue/yellow reflective ribbons and arrows. Marking is denser at unclear intersections and more sporadic where the way is obvious.
accessibilityNotes: SAT says Möja has many options for strollers, wheelchairs and limited-mobility visitors because ferries stop at Berg, Löka, Ramsmora and Långvik, and the SAT route is on gravel roads.
Do not promise full wheelchair accessibility without caveats: ferry boarding, quay conditions, vessel choice, water level, weather, gradients and loose gravel can matter.

sections.descriptionDraft: Möja is an easy but distinctive SAT section: about 13.8 km of mostly gravel/local road walking from Långvik through Ramsmora, Löka, Berg and Möjaström to Hamn, then back to Berg where the main services are. It is not a full island loop, and Hamn has no ferry quay or services. Treat the route as a multi-access linear section through living archipelago villages, with Berg/Kyrkviken as the primary public-service cluster and several other villages/quays useful for shorter variants.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Use Waxholmsbolaget/SL as the canonical access layer. SAT names five trail-relevant ferry stops: Långvik, Ramsmora, Löka, Berg and Möja Ström/Möjaström. Rechecked 2026-04-26 Europe/Stockholm: current static line/table 14A/14B is v14, valid 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-18 and 2026-08-17 to 2026-12-12; v12 is also current for those same spring/autumn windows and provides supplemental Möja access via Långvik/Dragedet. s14 still resolves to summer 2025, w14 expired 2026-04-01, and s40/Nord-Syd still resolves to summer 2025 even though SAT states Nord-Syd runs 2026-06-22 to 2026-08-16. Treat summer 2026 line 14 and Nord-Syd/line 40 as live-planner-only until current 2026 static tables appear; the stale s40 table serves Berg and Ramsmora on Möja, not all five SAT quays. Ticket wording must stay exact-date: all SL tickets cover the Stockholm-Vaxholm-area Waxholmsbolaget route year-round, but travel farther out toward Möja normally needs Waxholmsbolaget ticketing for the beyond-Vaxholm part unless the traveler has a qualifying SL period ticket during the low season, 14 September-29 April. Waxholmsbolaget tickets can be bought in the SL app. Do not present Strömma/Cinderella as static public hiker access to Möja. Current Strömma 2026 public timetable material exposes the Stockholm-Sandhamn route; the Möja dinner/Cinderella page is marked not available despite retaining old Möja-line text. Mention it only if exact-date booking later proves a usable Möja stop. Private operators such as Möja Båttaxi, Möja Outdoor, Gula Båten, Stavsnäs Båttaxi and Waxholm Water Taxi are fallback/charter options only when booked or quoted in advance and when weather/sea conditions allow; do not model them as scheduled public access. Watch timetable symbols: B/C and lowercase b require advance booking by the listed deadline, X means the quay is served without a fixed time, | means the quay is not served, a means alighting only, p means boarding only and z means reverse order. At semaphore piers, raise the semaphore so the Waxholmsbolaget boat knows to stop; in darkness, signal with a headlamp or flashlight. Semaphore use is separate from, and does not replace, any required advance booking.

sections.accessibilityDraft: Möja is one of the more accessible SAT sections by route surface because the official route is almost entirely gravel/local road and ferries stop at several villages. Still, do not mark the full journey as guaranteed wheelchair accessible: ferry boarding, water level, vessel type, quay conditions, weather, gradients, traffic and loose gravel can all affect access.
sections.campingRulesDraft: Do not expose a campsite on Möja. SAT FAQ states there are no campsites on Möja; older local folder wording about possible tenting near Dansbanan/Möja Gästhem is not strong enough for a mapped campsite and newer local service context is mixed. If one-night tenting under allemansrätten is mentioned, keep it general, outside homes/cultivated/sensitive land, jetties/boathouses and prohibited areas. Camping is prohibited in Möja-Björndalen nature reserve.

rulesDraft.camping: No official campsite/tent site should be exposed on Möja. One-night tenting may be mentioned only as general allemansrätten guidance outside homes, cultivated/sensitive land, jetties/boathouses and prohibited areas. Camping is prohibited in Möja-Björndalen nature reserve.
rulesDraft.fires: Do not expose a public firepit/grill. Fires should be limited to officially designated fire pits where present and allowed; never on rocks, terrain or beaches. Open fire is prohibited in Möja-Björndalen, and current fire bans override all static guidance.
rulesDraft.dogs: Use the stricter visitor-facing rule: dogs leashed March-September on SAT, and always leashed in Möja-Björndalen nature reserve.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Roland Svensson Museum
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Small art museum at Ramsmora brygga dedicated to archipelago artist and writer Roland Svensson. SAT explicitly calls it worth a visit; the museum says visits are possible year-round by booking and daily from midsummer in 2026.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Ramsmora fishing village and harbour
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Ramsmora harbour/village context near the ferry quay and Roland Svensson Museum. Treat as fishing-village heritage and route atmosphere, not as a fishing permission or public service claim.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Löka village
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Well-preserved village with turn-of-the-century character, narrow passages, close-set houses, small agricultural traces and stone-lined watercourses. Treat as village heritage context, not a single facility.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Berg / Kyrkviken
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Möja's largest village and service hub, with guest harbour, church, dance pavilion, local heritage museum, shop and food services nearby. Use as broad village/service heritage context.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Möja kyrka
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Church from 1768 on southern Stora Möja between Möjaström and Berg. Good high-confidence heritage stop near the service hub.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Möja Hembygdsmuseum
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Small local heritage museum uphill in Bergs by with 19th-century roots and views over Bergbofjärden. Add accessibility caveat in later integration because the museum itself may be difficult to access.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Möja Dansbana
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Outdoor dance pavilion just north of Berg. SAT mentions it before hikers reach Berg, and local sources describe it as a long-running cultural gathering place. Treat as heritage/culture POI, not shelter or rest facility.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Hamn
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Small secluded western-side hamlet by a natural harbour, with older houses descending toward the water and early-1900s village character. SAT says there are no ferry quay or services in Hamn, so this is heritage/narrative only.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Möja-Björndalen nature reserve
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Nearby nature-reserve and yellow-marked local nature-trail context around the Ramsmora-Hamn side of Möja. Keep separate from the SAT main gravel-road geometry and do not import reserve service icons as SAT facilities. Reserve rules prohibit camping and open fire and require leashed dogs/cats.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Långvik yttre bathing spot
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Natural bathing spot by Långvik outer harbour. Naturkartan/Värmdö describe a built beach west of the guest pier with an accessible ramp, but no HaV registered bathing-water status has been found; do not attach water-quality, lifeguard or toilet claims.

pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Informal natural bathing at Saltvik with rocks and sand beach. Local sources support bathing, but Visit Möja says Möja has no official bathing place and HaV does not list Saltvik as a registered monitored bathing water.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Möja research: official route facts and geometry, ferry/access layer, primary Berg services, food/shop candidates, heritage/nature POIs, protected-area rules and early integration traps.
keyFindings: SAT lists Möja as Easy 13.8 km, 4:30 hours and 85 m gain. The official PDF/Outdooractive export says moderate and 83 m gain/79 m descent; prefer SAT web/step-guide difficulty and keep the conflict.
The Möja section is not a full loop. The official route is Långvik to Ramsmora, Löka, Berg, Möjaström and Hamn, then back to Berg because Hamn has no ferry quay or services.

Official PDF/Outdooractive support 13.8 km and mostly road/gravel-road walking. OSM/Wikidata appear to undercount around 10.4 km, probably excluding the return-to-Berg portion or reflecting older geometry.
The main SAT access quays are Långvik, Ramsmora, Löka, Berg and Möja Ström/Möjaström. Do not promote Dragedet, Södermöja, Granholmen or Korsö as SAT section access just because line 14 serves them.

Waxholmsbolaget line/table 14A/14B is the main public access layer. v14 is current for 2 Apr-18 Jun 2026 and 17 Aug-12 Dec 2026, while s14 still resolves to summer 2025; summer 2026 needs live planning or later recheck.
Berg/Kyrkviken guest harbour is the strongest public hiker utility cluster: SAT confirms toilet and water there, not in winter.

Coop Berg is the strongest year-round shop. Coop Långvik, Jeppes, Möja Värdshus/Bageri, Les Poissonniers/Möja Fisk and Möja Hamnbar are useful food/service candidates, all with opening-hours, customer, app/payment or seasonality caveats.
Guest-harbour toilet/water/shower at Långvik, Löka and Möjaström should remain pending/conditional until hiker access, seasonality and payment are verified.
No campsite should be exposed. SAT/Visit Möja indicate no official campsite, and Möja-Björndalen reserve rules prohibit camping.
No public SAT firepit should be exposed in iteration 1. Reserve rules prohibit open fire and OSM/harbour grill hints need official/local verification.
Roland Svensson Museum is the strongest single heritage POI. Löka village, Berg/Kyrkviken, Möja kyrka, Möja Hembygdsmuseum and Hamn are strong heritage/context candidates.
Björndalen/naturstigen is valuable nearby nature context but should not be merged into SAT main-route geometry or facilities until later verification.
Bathing candidates such as Långvik and Saltvik are informal/unmonitored in iteration 1. Do not add HaV sampled-water-quality status.
Emergency/AED information belongs in emergencyMetadataDraft only and needs exact-coordinate/current-registry verification.

sections.descriptionDraft: Grinda is a moderate 9.8 km clockwise SAT island loop with a public start/end at Södra Grinda ferry quay and a natural service-hub start option at Grinda Wärdshus. The route mixes gravel road, forest road, pasture edges, shoreline walking and more technical rocky/rooty trail on the northern and eastern/southeastern coast. Treat it as a nature-reserve loop with excellent seasonal services, but with strict rules for camping, fire and dogs.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Use Waxholmsbolaget/SL and Strömma/Cinderella as separate access layers. SAT Grinda officially starts/ends at Södra Grinda ferry quay, while Norra Grinda is a secondary Waxholmsbolaget access point that can be useful for variants and exits. Grinda's operator says both Södra Grinda and Norra Grinda are searchable stops, Södra is the busiest, and both are about 10-15 minutes from Wärdshuset. Rechecked 2026-04-26 Europe/Stockholm: current Waxholmsbolaget v11 is valid 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-18 and 2026-08-17 to 2026-12-12 and is the strongest current evidence for both Södra Grinda and Norra Grinda in line 11A/11B patterns; v12/v13 include Södra Grinda in some tables but should not be used as evidence for Norra. Direct summer s11/s12/s13 PDFs still resolve to 2025, so use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning for roughly 2026-06-19 to 2026-08-16 until current 2026 summer static PDFs appear. Grinda is beyond the normal Stockholm-Vaxholm/Rindö SL-ticket area, so ordinary Grinda travel normally needs Waxholmsbolaget ticketing for the outer part; Grinda's operator says low-season travel 14 September to 29 April accepts SL period tickets valid 30 days or longer, which applied on the check date. Current Strömma/Cinderella 2026 Stockholm-Sandhamn material serves Södra Grinda only from 2026-04-30 to 2026-09-27 and uses separate Strömma tickets; no current Norra Grinda Cinderella evidence was found. Watch timetable symbols such as B/b/C/c request booking, X no fixed time, | not served, a alighting only, p boarding only and z reverse order. Raise the pier semaphore where required; this does not replace any required booking.

sections.campingRulesDraft: Grinda is a nature reserve. Camping/tenting should only be exposed at the designated paid campsite near Norra bryggan/camping area. Suppress wild/dispersed camping and any non-designated bivouac pins.

rulesDraft.reserve: Grinda is a nature reserve. Do not damage rock, soil, stone, trees, shrubs, mosses, lichens, herbs or other vegetation; do not disturb wildlife.
rulesDraft.dogs: Dogs must be leashed year-round in the reserve; use the Grinda-specific reserve rule over the less strict general SAT seasonal wording.
rulesDraft.camping: Camping is only allowed at the designated tent site near Norra bryggan/camping area.
rulesDraft.fires: Fires and grilling are only allowed at designated fire places. Never light fires or grill directly on rock, do not break branches or collect wood, and check current fire bans.
rulesDraft.waste: Use public/customer waste points only where allowed and take waste back where possible; island waste handling is limited.
rulesDraft.vehicles: Motor vehicles are not allowed except on designated roads/where permitted by reserve rules.
rulesDraft.boating: Boat anchoring is limited: no more than two consecutive days at the same shore, and no anchoring on shorelines marked as prohibited.

utilitiesDraft: SAT confirms toilets and water at the guest harbor and Grinda Sea Lodge, not during winter, but operator pages frame several utilities as seasonal, paid, harbor, lodging or customer services.

Länsstyrelsen explicitly says dry toilets exist at all bathing places and at Södra ångbåtsbryggan; iteration 3 keeps Södra water guarded and adds separate dry toilets for Södra, Källviken and Badviken/Norra.
Grinda Camping is the official/designated paid campsite with dry toilets, water pumps, waste handling, communal BBQ and high-season shower access via the guest-harbor service house.
Grinda Wärdshus, Lanthandel & Café, bakery, Framfickan, Sea Lodge, cottage village and guest-harbor services are seasonal, opening-hours dependent, customer/guest/fee-based or mixed-access.

Expose guest harbor and Sea Lodge toilet/water with not-winter plus fee/customer caveats; keep showers, electricity, waste, sauna, boat rentals, septic pump-out and many service-house details guarded unless later passes confirm broad public hiker access.
Default waste guidance should remain pack-out/mainland where possible; do not render customer/harbor environmental stations as ordinary trail litter service.
waterSourcesDraft: Water at the guest harbor, not during winter per SAT; operator price list frames canister refill as paid harbor service, so include fee/customer caveat.
Water at Grinda Sea Lodge, not during winter per SAT; operator pages do not clearly prove broad public hiker access, so include current-hours/customer caveat.
Water pumps at the paid campsite; verify season and whether they are for camping guests.
Do not render Södra, Källviken or Badviken/Norra beach/toilet-point water from OSM alone; official sources currently verify dry toilets/bathing places rather than public drinking taps.
Carry water outside the main season or when businesses/service points may be closed.

Showers and other harbor service-house features are customer/fee or seasonal metadata, not ordinary public trail utilities.

facilitiesDraft.name: Water at guest harbour
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal; SAT says water at guest harbor is not available in winter.
facilitiesDraft.feeContext: Operator price list lists canister refill max 10 liters at 2 SEK/l.
facilitiesDraft.confidenceMeaning: high confidence that water is present per SAT/operator sources; not high confidence that it is free or unconditional public hiker water
facilitiesDraft.description: SAT-confirmed water at the Hemviken/guest-harbor service hub, with operator material framing canister refill as a paid harbor service and fresh-water filling near piers. Verify current season, fee and service-house access before relying outside main season.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Sea Lodge toilet
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal; SAT says Sea Lodge toilet/water are not available in winter.
facilitiesDraft.description: SAT-confirmed open toilet at Grinda Sea Lodge on the southern/eastern side of the loop, not available in winter. Operator material supports Sea Lodge area toilets but frames many services in lodging/customer context, so current opening and public access should be checked.

facilitiesDraft.name: Water at Grinda Sea Lodge
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal; SAT says Sea Lodge toilet/water are not available in winter.
facilitiesDraft.description: SAT-confirmed water at Grinda Sea Lodge. Operator material supports running-water sinks in the Sea Lodge area but mostly in accommodation context, so verify current season/opening before relying outside the Midsummer-to-mid-August public service period.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Camping
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Paid camping season; shower access high season via guest-harbor service house.
facilitiesDraft.description: Designated paid campsite/tenting area. Official rules allow camping only at designated places; do not expose dispersed camping elsewhere on Grinda.

facilitiesDraft.name: Södra Grinda dry toilet
facilitiesDraft.description: Public dry toilet at/near Södra ångbåtsbryggan and Södra Grinda bathing area. Länsstyrelsen confirms dry toilets at all bathing places and at Södra ångbåtsbryggan; Explore Archipelago/Wikimedia/OSM secondary checks support this point.

facilitiesDraft.name: Källviken dry toilet
facilitiesDraft.description: Public dry toilet linked to Källviken bathing place. Länsstyrelsen confirms dry toilets at Grinda bathing places; Explore Archipelago service-map data and OSM secondary checks support this individual point. Do not infer drinking water from this toilet point.

facilitiesDraft.name: Badviken / Norra Grinda dry toilet
facilitiesDraft.description: Public dry toilet linked to the Badviken/Norra Grinda bathing area. Länsstyrelsen confirms dry toilets at Grinda bathing places; Explore Archipelago service-map data and OSM secondary checks support this individual point. Do not infer drinking water from this toilet point.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Wärdshus
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Year-round with variable opening/reservations; verify current hours.
facilitiesDraft.description: Main food/lodging anchor near the loop and natural mid-island start option. Treat hotel/lodging functions as service context, not trail utility.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Lanthandel & Café
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Spring-autumn with strongest service in high season; verify current hours.
facilitiesDraft.description: Shop/cafe/bakery service near Wärdshus, useful for groceries, picnic food, simple lunches and fresh bread when open.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Sea Lodge food service
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Public individual/family food service mainly Midsummer to mid-August; verify current opening.
facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal Sea Lodge food/lodging context with breakfast/lunch/dinner during individual/family periods. Other services such as showers, sauna and rentals are customer/paid metadata.

facilitiesDraft.name: Grinda Bakery
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal; official operator page says roughly Midsummer to mid-August, with current hours subject to change.
facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal bakery/Bageriboden by the guest-harbor side. Useful for bread and breakfast-style supplies when open; keep Lanthandeln as the broader shop/cafe service.

facilitiesDraft.name: Framfickan
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Seasonal harbor-side food service; verify current opening hours.
facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal drop-in/takeaway food service by the guest harbor. Treat as current-hours-required service rather than dependable year-round resupply.

facilitiesDraft.name: Södra Grinda ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Primary SAT Grinda trailhead and loop start/end. Transit fallback only; prefer accessMetadataDraft for rendering.

facilitiesDraft.name: Norra Grinda ferry quay
facilitiesDraft.description: Secondary Waxholmsbolaget access near the northern loop. Transit fallback only; verify current timetable and prefer accessMetadataDraft for rendering.

facilitiesDraft.name: Designated fire area by camping
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Only when no fire ban; use designated fire places only.
facilitiesDraft.description: Designated fire/grill place by the tent site/camping area. Never imply fires are allowed outside designated places, and fire bans override static guidance.

facilitiesDraft.name: Designated fire area near southern services
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: Only when no fire ban; use designated fire places only.
facilitiesDraft.description: Designated fire/grill place at/near Södra Grinda. Never imply fires are allowed outside designated places, and fire bans override static guidance.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Grinda naturreservat
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Reserve-wide context for the SAT Grinda loop. Grinda has been protected since 2000, covers about 503 ha total / 178 ha land, and is owned/managed by Skärgårdsstiftelsen; strict reserve rules govern camping, fire, dogs, vegetation, wildlife, vehicles and anchoring.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Klubbuddens utsiktsplats / Klubbudden viewpoint
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Highest-point/view highlight on the eastern/southeastern technical part of the loop; Länsstyrelsen names Klubbudden as the island's about 35 m high viewpoint and Explore Archipelago has a service-map viewpoint at this coordinate. Treat as one viewpoint-style attraction, not a separate summit plus viewpoint pair.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Northwest viewpoint
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Generic north/west/Hemviken-side viewpoint candidate. Do not rename this to Lilla utsikten; iteration 4 found Lilla utsikten is a different, secondary/guarded OSM/Komoot candidate.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Källviken beach
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Sand beach/bathing cove, with Länsstyrelsen noting accessible entrance context. A separate Källviken dry-toilet facility is modeled in facilitiesDraft. Observe reserve rules and fire restrictions.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Badviken beach
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: North-side bathing POI near the northern access/service context. Länsstyrelsen and Explore Archipelago identify this as one of the primary bathing places, and a separate Badviken/Norra dry-toilet facility is modeled in facilitiesDraft.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Södra Grinda beach
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Child-friendly southern swimming near Södra bryggan and the SAT start/end side. Länsstyrelsen notes accessible water-entry context at Södra bryggan.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Grinda Lantbruk
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Farm/cultural-landscape context where grazing animals help maintain the reserve landscape. It is a valid nearby context point but not directly on the SAT line; do not confuse with mainland Grinda Säteri search results.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Grinda nature and culture trail
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Secondary about 2.5 km nature/culture trail context around southeast Grinda, starting at gården Hemviken per Länsstyrelsen. Coordinate is only an approximate Hemviken/Wärdshus-area anchor and should not be used as an exact trailhead without better source data.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Lilla utsikten
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Named by OSM and mentioned by Komoot as signed from the main trail, but not verified in official SAT, Länsstyrelsen or Explore Archipelago sources. Keep as secondary/optional viewpoint candidate only.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Grinda Wärdshus heritage context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Art Nouveau villa/landmark and service hub with early-1900s heritage context. Merge this description into the Grinda Wärdshus food/service facility in final integration to avoid a duplicate marker.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Grinda research: official route facts and geometry conflicts, ferry/access layer, core public services, reserve rules, POIs and safe integration shape.
keyFindings: Use current official SAT web/step-guide scalar facts as canonical for iteration 1: Moderate, 9.8 km, 3:30 and 55 m gain.
Model Grinda as a clockwise loop. The official step guide starts/ends at Grinda Södra ferry quay; the section page describes Grinda Wärdshus as a natural start option.

Official geometry artifacts conflict with current public text: linked GPX computes to about 8.87 km from 621 trackpoints, Outdooractive lists 8.9 km/94 m ascent and older official PDF lists 8.1 km/138 m ascent.
Route character is mixed: gravel road, forest road, pasture edges, shoreline paths and more technical rocky/rooty trail on the northern and eastern/southeastern coast.

Access layer is centered on Södra Grinda and Norra Grinda. Södra is the SAT start/end and is served by Waxholmsbolaget plus current 2026 Strömma/Cinderella Stockholm-Sandhamn material; Norra is secondary and requires live timetable verification.

Current Waxholmsbolaget v11 is valid for 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-18 and 2026-08-17 to 2026-12-12. v12/v13 also show Södra Grinda in some supplemental patterns; direct s11/s13 summer PDFs still resolve to 2025.

Grinda is beyond the normal Stockholm-Vaxholm/Rindö SL-ticket area; Waxholmsbolaget tickets are normally needed for the outer part unless low-season long-period SL ticket rules apply. Strömma requires separate tickets.
SAT confirms toilet and water at guest harbor and Sea Lodge, not in winter. These are the strongest utility candidates for iteration 1.
Grinda Camping is the designated paid camping/tenting area. Wild/dispersed camping should be suppressed because reserve rules allow camping only at designated places.
Grinda Wärdshus, Lanthandel & Café and Sea Lodge are useful food/service nodes with seasonality or opening-hour caveats. Lodging/customer functions should remain context or guarded metadata.
Reserve rules are central: dogs leashed, fires/grilling only at designated places, no fires on rock, no wood collection/damage, and current fire bans override static guidance.
Expose representative swimming POIs at Källviken, Badviken/north side and Södra Grinda, but avoid unverified water-quality/lifeguard claims.
Expose reserve/cultural POIs conservatively: Grinda nature reserve, Klubbudden viewpoint, generic northwest viewpoint, Grinda Lantbruk, Grinda Wärdshus heritage and nature/culture trail context.

Keep individual firepits, customer showers/sauna/electricity/waste, septic pump-out, Södra/stugby toilet/water candidates and service-house details pending or suppressed until later passes verify public hiker access.
