pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Södra Fladen wetland and bird tower
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Route-side wetland created by Haninge/Initiativ Utö work, with a bird tower/rest area; SAT describes rainwater purification, fish spawning and bird life here.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Rävstavik cliff bathing and east-coast viewpoint
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Named SAT route location on the technical eastern coast, with rocky shoreline, sea views, cliff bathing and slippery-rock warning when wet. Import as scenic/bathing context rather than an easy-access beach; iteration 4 specifically flags deep water, harder water access and slippery rocks as safety context for less confident swimmers.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Barnens bad
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Shallow sandy beach north of Gruvbyn on/near the final SAT segment. Länsstyrelsen and Utö pages describe it as an easy, child-friendly beach/rest area. Iteration 3 keeps this as the normal beach POI and splits the toilet and fire/rest/waste details into separate facility/guarded records; iteration 4 removed the brittle Naturkartan deep link from the active source list.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Utö mines and mining heritage
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Water-filled mine shafts, mining boards and museum/heritage context near Gruvbyn. SAT and Länsstyrelsen emphasize Utö's 700-year mining history; Länsstyrelsen asks visitors to leave stones/minerals in place. Iteration 2 moved this to secondary/detour context because the current SAT GPX does not pass directly through the museum/mines cluster.

pointsOfInterestDraft.name: Utö kvarn
pointsOfInterestDraft.description: Historic windmill above Gruvbyn, built in 1791 per Länsstyrelsen and identified as a viewpoint/cultural landmark in OSM/Naturkartan context. Iteration 2 moved this to secondary/detour context due to route distance.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Russian baking oven / Ryssungnar side curiosity
secondaryPoiDraft.description: SAT step guide says a Russian baking oven from the 1700s is signposted down to the right, but hikers should stay on the SAT marked trail to the left. Keep as context, not normal POI.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Utö mines and Gruvmuseet secondary context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Iteration 2 geometry found the mines/Gruvmuseet cluster is about 311 m from the current SAT GPX, so keep the heritage content as secondary/detour context unless a later heritage layer accepts nearby POIs.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Utö kvarn secondary context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Iteration 2 geometry found Utö kvarn is about 206 m off the current SAT GPX. It remains strong heritage/viewpoint context but should not be a normal on-route POI by default.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Kroka / Järnholmssund detour context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: SAT notes Järnholmssund as a worthwhile detour if continuing straight at Kroka, but the marked SAT turns left.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Storsand / southern Utö context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Utö.se praises Storsand, but notes the area belongs to Utö shooting field and access must be checked. Do not import as a SAT route facility.

pendingFacilityDraft.description: Iteration 2 promoted the toilet component as sat-uto-ravstavik-north-toilet after GPX proximity review. pendingFacilityDraft.name: Södra Fladen rest area, shelter and fire pit
pendingFacilityDraft.description: Iteration 2 promoted the grouped rest-area record as sat-uto-sodra-fladen-rest-area. Iteration 4 confirms the rest/shelter/bench function can remain normal, but this guarded duplicate should carry the fireplace/fire-ban subfacility review.

pendingFacilityDraft.name: Utö Camping service building
pendingFacilityDraft.description: Service cottage with toilets, showers and simple kitchen belongs to the paid campsite and should not appear as a generic public route toilet/shower/kitchen.

pendingFacilityDraft.name: Barnens bad fire/rest/waste cluster
pendingFacilityDraft.description: Iteration 3 split Barnens bad into beach POI sat-uto-barnens-bad, normal toilet sat-uto-barnens-bad-toilet, and this guarded fire/rest/waste context. Iteration 4 keeps grill/rest/waste conditional because the Naturkartan deep link is brittle and SAT asks hikers to carry garbage back where possible. pendingFacilityDraft.name: Utö Värdshus defibrillator candidate
pendingFacilityDraft.description: Hjärtstartarregistret/OpenAEDMap/Wikimedia evidence indicates a defibrillator at Utö Värdshus reception, registry id 23722. Keep as emergency metadata only until current public access and opening-hour details are verified; do not import as a normal trail facility.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Spränga Brygga service suppression
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: SAT explicitly says Spränga Brygga has no services; do not infer services from ferry access.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Harbor marine-only service suppression
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Sewage pump-out, fuel, marina power, boat berths, harbor laundry and similar marine services should stay out of hiking import unless the app gains a marine layer.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Unverified Utö water-pump suppression
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Do not import OSM-only water pumps as drinking water; at least one is tagged not potable and others are conditional/unspecified.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Wild camping suppression

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Storsand route-facility suppression
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Storsand is off the SAT loop and tied to southern Utö shooting-field access constraints; keep as side context only.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: 112 emergency response from island
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: For serious illness or injury call 112, state exact location/GPS and that the incident is on Utö. SAT FAQ notes resources may be sent from the mainland.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: Utö Värdshus AED context
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: Registered AED context at Utö Värdshus reception, with Hjärtstartarregistret id 23722 also mirrored in OpenAEDMap/Wikimedia evidence. Keep as emergency metadata rather than a normal route facility unless the app gains an emergency layer and current public access/hours are rechecked.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: Main emergency access points
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: Gruvbryggan and Spränga Brygga are the ferry access points most likely to matter for evacuation/logistics; exact response is determined by 112/SOS.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Technical east-coast trail
safetyWarningsDraft.description: SAT identifies the hill from Gruvbryggan past the inn toward Rävstavik and north along the eastern coast to Kroka as the most technical section; rocks can be slippery when wet.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Mining landscape caution
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Water-filled historical mining pits and mineral-rich spoil heaps are a key heritage feature near Gruvbyn; Länsstyrelsen asks visitors to leave stones and minerals in place.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Bathing and algal bloom context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: SAT FAQ notes Baltic algal blooms can make green/murky water unsafe in summer; Rävstavik is cliff/deep-water context while Barnens bad is shallow sandy beach.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Ticks and adders
safetyWarningsDraft.description: SAT FAQ identifies ticks and adders as the main wildlife/health cautions in the archipelago; consider TBE prevention and check for ticks after hiking.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Utö pass across route geometry, public and commercial facilities, access logistics, reserve/safety/emergency rules and app import shape.
keyFindings: Utö should be represented as a counterclockwise challenging loop with a dense Gruvbryggan service cluster and a no-service Spränga alternate trailhead.
Official distance evidence conflicts: section summary says 18.4 km, while step guide/PDF/Outdooractive/OSM indicate about 16.7-16.8 km.
Strong normal facility candidates from iteration 1 are the Gruvbryggan public WC, Utö Camping as a paid designated campsite, ICA Utö Livs, Hamnboden cafe/kiosk and Utö Bakgård bakery.
The guest harbor has showers, sauna, water, waste and marina services, but much of that is paid/customer/marine-oriented and should remain grouped/conditional rather than normal hiking facilities.
Södra Fladen wetland, Rävstavik, Barnens bad, Gruvbyn mines and Utö kvarn are the main POI candidates; Ryssungnar, Järnholmssund and Storsand remain secondary context.
Reserve rules are strict: no camping except designated places, fire only at prepared/designated sites, dog leash rules and no damage to geology/vegetation.
Water pumps are suppressed/pending because OSM records include not-potable, conditional or unspecified status.
Access metadata is strong for line 21 and bus 846 outside the summer gap; exact summer 2026 and Nordsyd times need live or later timetable validation.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 2 should pin Barnens bad beach/toilet/fireplace coordinates separately and decide whether any of them can be normal facilities.
Iteration 2 should resolve Rävstavik toilet proximity and whether it belongs to SAT or a side/north loop context.
Iteration 2 should decide how to represent commercial food/lodging/rental services in the app's current schema.
Iteration 2 should re-check Utö water/refill claims from direct official public-hiker sources.
Later iterations should revalidate Nordsyd and summer 2026 line 21/19/20 timetables.

Södra Fladen rest area was promoted as a normal grouped outdoor facility candidate because SAT places the bird tower, fire pit, small shelter and benches there, and OSM pins the shelter cluster about 12 m from the current GPX.

Barnens bad / Norra Sand was promoted as a normal grouped beach/rest/toilet/fire context. The beach/rest centroid and toilet should still be split during app integration if the schema supports subpoints.
Rävstavik north skärgårdsmaja was promoted as a normal toilet candidate after Naturkartan plus OSM and GPX proximity checks; a separate south Rävstavik OSM-only toilet remains pending.

Hamnboden and Utö Bakgård were demoted from normal standalone candidates to conditional/commercial cluster records because current opening-hour evidence is seasonal and the old Bakgård domain appears unsafe to use.
Mines/Gruvmuseet and Kvarnen were moved to secondary context because iteration 2 measured them about 311 m and 206 m from the current SAT GPX, respectively.
Access evidence was strengthened: line 21, line 19, line 20 and SL bus 846 have current non-summer 2026 PDFs, but Nordsyd/line 40 exact 2026 times remain live/current-planner evidence only.

Safety metadata was strengthened with reserve/Natura 2000 facts, live fire-ban guidance, Utö shooting-field warnings, mine/rock hazards, algal bloom context, ticks/adders, 112 island response and pending AED registry verification.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 3 should independently re-check the current SAT GPX source path and preserve enough provenance that later integrators can reproduce the 18.42 km measurement.
Iteration 3 should verify whether Barnens bad should stay one grouped outdoor facility or split into separate beach, toilet, fire/rest and waste records.
Iteration 3 should revalidate Rävstavik north vs south toilet naming and public-status evidence without relying only on OSM for the south toilet.
Iteration 3 should decide whether ICA remains the only normal commercial resupply marker and whether other food services stay cluster-only.
Later iterations should continue checking Nordsyd/line 40 current 2026 exact times and AED registry/open-access evidence.

iterationSummaries.focus: Third Utö pass across reproducible H25 GPX provenance, Barnens bad split, Rävstavik toilet confidence, commercial-service currentness, access/safety/emergency pressure testing and JSON QA.
keyFindings: GPX provenance was fully reproduced: SAT Utö page links Google Drive file 1SiHBiKvOTbvOyUe_xHxYfqBmQk1JNWdn, direct download works, metadata/trk name is SAT Utö H25, timestamp 2025-10-20T10:12:09.494Z, 1,893 trackpoints, 18.422 km 2D length.

Route proximity against H25 was tightened: Södra Fladen rest cluster about 9.8 m from GPX, Barnens bad beach about 39.1 m, Barnens bad toilet about 0.7 m, Rävstavik north toilet/waste about 1.6 m and Rävstavik bathing/fire/view context about 2.8 m.

Barnens bad was split to avoid duplicate normal records: sat-uto-barnens-bad remains the normal beach POI, sat-uto-barnens-bad-toilet is the normal toilet facility, and sat-uto-barnens-bad-toilet-fireplace remains guarded fire/rest/waste context with fire-ban caveats.

Rävstavik north skärgårdsmaja remains a strong normal toilet candidate through Naturkartan, OSM checked data and Commons 2025 photo evidence. The south Rävstavik toilet remains pending because non-OSM corroboration is weak.

Commercial services were pressure-tested: ICA remains the only strong normal commercial resupply candidate; Utö Camping remains a normal paid campsite. Hamnboden, Utö Bakgård, Seglarbaren, Utö Värdshus, Vandrarhemmet, rentals and Aktiv Skärgård should stay commercial/conditional or cluster-only.

iterationSummaries.focus: Fourth Utö pass focused on brittle/dead source remediation, fire/rest/waste import policy, Rävstavik and Barnens bad confidence, access/emergency currentness and JSON decision QA.
keyFindings: Several Naturkartan object/deep links for Barnens bad and Rävstavik returned raw HTTP 404 even though search-index evidence still exposed the content. These links were demoted to brittle evidence and removed from Barnens active normal source lists.

Barnens bad remains split: beach POI and toilet are normal candidates, while grill/rest/waste stays guarded context because fire use is rule-dependent and SAT encourages hikers to take garbage back to the mainland.

descriptionDraft.short: A short, easy gravel-road connector between the Utö and Ålö SAT sections, controlled by firing-range stay-on-road rules rather than facilities.
descriptionDraft.long: The Utö - Ålö Connector follows a gravel road from Gula Villan on Utö to just south of Ålö Bridge, passing through an active military firing range. It is intentionally unmarked because hikers must stay on the road at all times. Use it as a practical link between sections; services are reached by continuing north toward Gruvbryggan or south toward Ålö brygga/Båtshaket, not on the connector itself.
doNotOverstate: Do not present the connector as a normal facility-rich hiking section.
Do not encourage side trips off the gravel road through the military firing range.
Do not import Ålö ferry-quay, Båtshaket or Ålö Storsand services as on-connector facilities.
Do not import the private/uncertain pump near Ålö Bridge as public drinking water.

gettingThereDraft.primaryContinuity: Walk the connector as the road link between the Utö and Ålö SAT sections.
gettingThereDraft.northAccess: Utö/Gruvbryggan and Spränga access belongs primarily to the Utö section but matters for connector logistics.
gettingThereDraft.southAccess: Ålö brygga/Båtshaket and line 22 are Ålö access context beyond the connector endpoint.
gettingThereDraft.seasonal: Nordsyd/line 40 can support summer island hopping, but exact times should be checked live and not frozen from stale 2025 sheets.

accessibilityDraft.summary: SAT says the gravel road between Utö and Ålö is accessible to everyone. Treat this as road-level accessibility, not a guarantee of full step-free public transport or facility access at both ends.

sections.userExperienceDraft: Mostly flat, road-based walking on dirt/gravel road. Easy underfoot and accessible compared with the surrounding island trails, but the experience is controlled by military-area rules rather than normal hiking exploration. Expect a clear road, bridge/road transition between Utö and Ålö, possible cyclists and local/service traffic, and no verified public facilities directly on the connector.
sections.rulesNarrativeDraft: Stay on the gravel road until the next SAT section. The military firing range lies on both sides of the road; current Försvarsmakten notices, signs, barriers and on-site boards override cached trail data. Dogs must be leashed and camping is not allowed along the connector road.
sections.serviceNarrativeDraft: No normal connector facilities should be imported. Carry water/snacks. Utö-side services belong to Gruvbryggan/Gruvbyn records; Ålö-side ferry, Båtshaket and beach facilities belong to Ålö records or access metadata.

accessMetadataDraft.description: Bike rental/return between Utö/Gruvbryggan and Ålö/Båtshaket can matter for logistics, but SAT is researched here as a walking connector and cycling services are paid/seasonal.

privateFallbackDraft.name: Private boat fallback context
privateFallbackDraft.description: BOUT and local sjötaxi/sjötransport operators may support private fallback logistics around Utö/Ålö. Do not present as public scheduled transport.

rulesDraft.name: Active firing-range road rule
rulesDraft.description: The connector road passes through or alongside Utö's active military firing range. SAT says hikers must stay on the gravel road; on-site signs, barriers and current Försvarsmakten notices override cached data. Do not imply the road is always passable during activity: if a barrier is lowered or the field is avlyst, do not pass.

rulesDraft.name: No camping along connector road
rulesDraft.description: SAT explicitly says camping is not allowed along the connector road. Adjacent reserve rules also restrict camping to designated or limited contexts.

rulesDraft.name: Dogs leashed on connector
rulesDraft.description: SAT says dogs must be leashed on the connector; Utö and Ålö-Rånö reserve contexts also support leash caution.

rulesDraft.name: No connector fireplace confirmed
rulesDraft.description: No fireplace was verified on the connector. Fires in adjacent reserves are allowed only at designated places and live fire bans override stored route notes.

serviceClustersDraft.name: Gula Villan start landmark and lodging context
serviceClustersDraft.description: Gula Villan is the named Utö-side connector start landmark and commercial lodging/hostel context. Do not import as a normal connector facility without current lodging availability review.

serviceClustersDraft.name: Ålö brygga service context
serviceClustersDraft.description: Ålö ferry-quay toilet and water are strong Ålö access/service evidence but sit about 2.2 km south of the connector endpoint. Keep as endpoint context and likely Ålö-section data, not normal connector facilities.

serviceClustersDraft.name: Båtshaket seasonal service context
serviceClustersDraft.description: Båtshaket at/near Ålö brygga is a summer restaurant and bike-rental/customer-service context beyond the connector endpoint. Treat as conditional Ålö access context, not a durable connector facility.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Ålö Bridge connector board
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Connector information/board context just south of Ålö Bridge, about 17 m from the GPX endpoint; nearby guidepost is about 4 m from the endpoint. Keep as future wayfinding/orientation metadata rather than a service facility or normal POI.

secondaryPoiDraft.name: Ålö Storsand off-connector context
secondaryPoiDraft.description: Ålö Storsand beach, toilet, water and barbecue evidence is strong for the Ålö section, but it is about 2.7-2.8 km from the connector endpoint and should not be imported under this connector except as future Ålö-section context.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress private/uncertain Ålö Bridge pump
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Hand pump near Ålö Bridge. No official SAT, Länsstyrelsen, Naturkartan, municipal or local confirmation found that it is public/potable for hikers. OSM marks access as private and notes it is only sometimes signed as okay to use; Commons photo also labels it probably private.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress wild camping along connector
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: SAT explicitly prohibits camping along the connector road; do not infer wild-camping opportunities from road/forest context.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress unverified connector fireplaces
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: No connector fireplace was verified in iteration 1. Do not import fire sites without a specific durable source and live fire-ban caveat.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress off-road POIs through firing range
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Because SAT says hikers must stay on the road through the firing range, do not import off-road curiosities or side-trip POIs from maps/blogs unless an official later route permits them.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress military-area access
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Do not present military training areas on either side of the road as accessible recreation space; on-site boards, barriers and live notices control.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: Remote island emergency response
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: For acute emergencies call 112 and provide exact location/GPS. Maritime rescue also routes through 112; response times and access depend on island conditions.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: No verified AED on connector
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: Iteration 1 found no verified AED directly on the connector. Hjärtstartarregistret/OpenAEDMap sources here refer to off-connector Utö Värdshus/Gruvbyn context and should not create a connector AED marker unless later connector-specific access is verified.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Stay on gravel road
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Primary connector warning: stay on the gravel road through the firing-range area. This should be shown more prominently than any POI/facility layer.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Military activity and unknown-object caution
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Use cautious military-area wording: never pass a lowered barrier, do not cross barriers or signs, and do not touch ammunition or unknown objects. Current Försvarsmakten notices and site boards override cached route data.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Barriers and ammunition warning
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Never pass a lowered barrier, even if no general access prohibition appears to be in force. Do not touch ammunition, projectiles or unknown objects. Local signs, boards and barriers override cached trail data.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Shared gravel road
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Connector follows a gravel road likely shared with cyclists, locals or service traffic; keep as route-safety metadata, not a facility.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Ticks and TBE context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: TBE/tick risk is relevant for Stockholm coastal and archipelago environments, but this is regional health metadata rather than a connector-specific facility.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Algal bloom bathing context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Use only if endpoint/nearby bathing context is shown; algal-bloom information is live/currentness-sensitive and should be checked near visit date.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Adder first-aid context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: General archipelago/nature warning only; use first-aid guidance rather than treating this as route-specific proof of adders.

notesDraft: Iteration 1 found the connector should be treated as a no-service continuity/safety section, not a facility-rich trail section.
The English official URL is /section/uto-alo-connector-2/; the non-2 URL currently resolves to Swedish/localized content.
Facilities at Ålö brygga, Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand are useful future Ålö-section context but should not be normal connector imports.
Försvarsmakten weekly/current notices can rotate. Store stable parent pages and require current on-site/live checks for restrictions.
Outdooractive, SAT GPX, Google My Maps and the SAT print PDF appear to share route provenance, so they corroborate geometry but are not fully independent.
Iteration 2 confirmed Gula Villan may remain connector start context, but Gruvbryggan/Spränga are Utö-owned access/services and Ålö brygga/Båtshaket/Storsand are Ålö-owned records.
Iteration 2 confirmed the Ålö Bridge pump is a real near-corridor feature but private/uncertain; keep it pending/suppressed and out of normal water import.
Iteration 2 confirmed the connector road should not be described as always passable during firing-range activity; barriers, current notices and on-site information override cached route data.
Iteration 3 found no official/local confirmation that the Ålö Bridge pump is public or potable; it was moved from pending water to explicit suppression.
Iteration 3 moved the Ålö Bridge board from secondary POI candidate to future wayfinding/orientation metadata only.
Iteration 3 confirmed the connector copy should stay functional and caution-forward: a practical road link, not a scenic or facility-rich section.
Iteration 4 confirmed official SAT pages, PDF, GPX and KML remain live and match the stored connector facts.
Iteration 4 reinforced the current-notice pattern for Utö skjutfält: stable parent pages plus dated weekly PDFs, with local barriers and boards overriding cached trail data.
Iteration 4 found HiiKER and Komoot too weak or derivative for connector facility claims; they remain source-caveat context only.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Utö - Ålö Connector pass across official route facts, geometry, facilities/services, access logistics, rules/safety/emergency and outdoor-guide/map corroboration.
keyFindings: The English official page is https://stockholmarchipelagotrail.com/section/uto-alo-connector-2/; the non-2 URL resolves to Swedish/localized content, so both URLs are stored explicitly.
The connector is 4.6 km, easy, about 90 minutes, with 29 m ascent and 28 m descent from the print PDF/Outdooractive evidence.
Current SAT-hosted and Drive GPX evidence names the route Utö Ålö SAT Trail connector, has 221 points and measures about 4.555 km from [58.954492,18.282835] to [58.934244,18.223116].
No normal public toilet, water, food, shelter, rest area, fireplace or camping facility was verified directly on the connector proper.
The route should be modeled primarily as continuity/access/safety metadata because SAT says it follows gravel road through an active military firing range and users must stay on the road.
Gula Villan, Ålö brygga/Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand are useful endpoint or adjacent-section context only, not normal connector facilities.
Ålö Bridge trail board/information context is a good secondary endpoint record, corroborated by OSM and Wikimedia photo evidence.
Private/uncertain pump near Ålö Bridge should stay pending/suppressed because OSM indicates private/uncertain access.
Rules metadata should include active firing-range road-only warning, no camping along the road, dogs leashed, no connector fireplace and live fire-ban caveats.
Emergency metadata should avoid showing any AED on the connector; prior Utö Värdshus AED context belongs to Utö/Gruvbyn unless later connector-specific access is verified.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 2 should independently re-check whether the connector has any truly public on-route facility, especially water/toilet claims near Ålö Bridge.
Iteration 2 should verify the exact official URL behavior and whether the English -2 slug remains stable.
Iteration 2 should check current Försvarsmakten Utö notices/feed structure and whether a stable RSS/current-notice URL should be stored.
Iteration 2 should decide whether the Ålö Bridge trail board should remain secondary context or be omitted from app import entirely.
Later iterations should reconcile endpoint service records with the forthcoming Ålö section to avoid duplication.

iterationSummaries.focus: Second Utö - Ålö Connector pass challenging the no-facility conclusion, route-source stability, firing-range current notices, endpoint ownership boundaries and JSON/app import shape.
keyFindings: The no-normal-facility conclusion still holds. The only real on-corridor near-hit was the Ålö Bridge pump, but OSM and Commons indicate private/uncertain access, so it remains pending/suppressed.
Gula Villan may remain a guarded connector start landmark/lodging context because SAT names it as the start, but it is a commercial guest facility rather than a normal public trail facility.
Gruvbryggan/Spränga access and services belong to the Utö section, while Ålö brygga, Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand belong to the Ålö section. Connector records now carry dedupe/handoff guidance.
Ålö ferry-quay service context, Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand were removed from connector candidate buckets and placed in additional reviewed metadata so they do not render as connector imports.
The English /section/uto-alo-connector-2/ page, Swedish URL and SAT-hosted GPX remain stable; the non-2 URL resolves to Swedish content and should not be the English officialUrl.
SAT-hosted GPX and Drive GPX are live and byte-identical. The GPX measures 4.555 km 2D, 4.558 km with raw elevation, with elevation range about 7-24.5 m.
Google My Maps KML is live but should be parsed using the Tourgeometrie placemark only, not flattened across all coordinates.
Outdooractive route 302291662 remains useful provenance but direct web access returned 403, so it should not be relied on as a live app-facing source.
Försvarsmakten Utö parent page is durable; the candidate RSS feed URL returned 404 and weekly PDFs rotate. Store parent pages plus a dated current-week PDF note only.
Firing-range wording was tightened: do not imply the road is always passable. If a barrier is lowered or the field is avlyst, current notices and on-site information override cached route data.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 3 should independently verify whether the Ålö Bridge pump has any non-OSM public-use confirmation or should move from pending to explicit suppression.
Iteration 3 should re-check Försvarsmakten current-notice discovery without relying on the 404 feed URL.
Iteration 3 should decide whether the Ålö Bridge information board should stay as secondary context or be omitted from any app import surface.
Later iterations should continue ensuring Ålö-side services are handed off to sat-alo rather than rendered under the connector.

iterationSummaries.focus: Third Utö - Ålö Connector pass on Ålö Bridge pump suppression, Försvarsmakten current-notice durability, Ålö Bridge board bucket, user-facing connector narrative and JSON QA.
keyFindings: No reliable non-OSM/non-Commons confirmation was found that the Ålö Bridge pump is public or potable. SAT, Länsstyrelsen, Naturkartan and local pages omit it, while OSM/Commons indicate private/probably private access.
The Ålö Bridge pump was moved from pending water to explicit suppression with high confidence for suppression; Komoot user-generated mention is not strong enough to override private-access caveats.
Försvarsmakten Utö skjutfält parent and general rules pages remain the durable sources. Multiple RSS/feed guesses returned 404 and week PDFs rotate, with only v17/v18 live in the iteration-3 scan.
The current-week v18 PDF was treated only as dated evidence for 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-03. App-facing guidance should remain parent-page/current-notice/on-site-sign based.
Ålö Bridge board/guidepost evidence is strong and close to the endpoint, but it is wayfinding metadata rather than a secondary POI. It moved to futureMetadataOnlyRecords.
The connector description was tightened to a practical road-link narrative: mostly flat gravel road, accessible underfoot, but governed by firing-range rules and lacking verified public facilities.
JSON QA found no missing decision IDs, duplicate IDs, guarded records in normal buckets or unguarded metadata records; appImportPreviewDraft remains intentionally empty.
Ålö-side records remain additional reviewed handoff metadata only, not connector candidates.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 4 should do a final source-currentness sweep for official SAT/GPX/PDF, Försvarsmakten parent/current notices and local endpoint pages.
Iteration 4 should review whether any connector metadata is still too broad or should be deferred entirely to sat-uto or sat-alo.
Iteration 4 should verify that the explicit pump suppression and wayfinding-board metadata do not accidentally create rendered connector items.

iterationSummaries.focus: Fourth Utö - Ålö Connector pass on official-source currentness, section-boundary handoffs, military-area safety/current notices, community-source quality and JSON import QA.
keyFindings: Official English and Swedish SAT connector pages, the SAT print PDF, SAT-hosted GPX, Drive direct GPX and Google My Maps KML remained live in the iteration-4 checks.
Stored route facts still match current official evidence: 4.6 km, about 1:30 h, 29 m ascent, 28 m descent, easy/T1, with GPX start [58.954492,18.282835] and end [58.934244,18.223116].
The SAT-hosted GPX and Google Drive direct GPX were confirmed byte-identical; the KML Tourgeometrie line measures about 4.556 km and should remain corroboration rather than override.
Outdooractive route id 302291662 is still useful as provenance through the SAT-linked share URL, but bare canonical access remains brittle and should not be a durable app-facing source.
No credible community, guide, forum or outdoor-guide source contradicted the no-normal-facility connector model.
HiiKER contains noisy/derivative facility-ish language and Komoot contains a weak user-generated pump tip; neither should promote connector facilities or public drinking water.
Ålö-owned records were hardened as handoff-only context for sat-alo, while Gruvbryggan/Årsta access was marked shared with sat-uto.
A separate high-priority barriers/ammunition warning was added so current on-site boards, lowered barriers and unknown-object/ammunition cautions are not lost inside general firing-range metadata.
JSON QA kept normalFacilityCandidates, normalPoiCandidates and appImportPreviewDraft empty. additionalMetadataRecordsReviewed is explicitly non-rendering handoff context.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 5 should be a final adversarial check that no guarded connector metadata can accidentally render as normal facilities or POIs.
Iteration 5 should re-check whether the high-priority safety copy duplicates or conflicts with the general firing-range warning.
Iteration 5 should confirm the connector can close with an intentionally empty preview before moving to the Ålö section.

iterationSummaries.focus: Final Utö - Ålö Connector adversarial closeout across import safety, military-area currentness, section-boundary handoffs, geometry/source currentness and JSON QA.
keyFindings: All five final checks agreed that normalFacilityCandidates, normalPoiCandidates and appImportPreviewDraft should remain empty.

Official EN/SV pages, SAT PDF, SAT-hosted GPX, Drive GPX, Google My Maps KML and the Outdooractive share route were live and still support the stored 4.6 km, 1:30 h, 29 m ascent and 28 m descent facts.
SAT-hosted and Drive GPX files were verified byte-identical with SHA-256 f2bc346c1f964e50713b234364f4618b1805546e3ea5359922f6b99f5b88092b.

Final geometry QA measured the GPX at 221 points, 4.555 km 2D, 4.558 km with raw elevation, start [58.954492,18.282835], end [58.934244,18.223116], and elevation range 7-24.5 m. KML longest track measured about 4.556 km.
The official ascent/descent should stay 29 m / 28 m; raw GPX point-to-point ascent around 65 m appears noisy and should not override official values.

Försvarsmakten week-18 PDF was live for 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-03 and found no access prohibition for that period, but reinforced that information boards, barriers and current notices override cached trail data. The guessed week-19 PDF returned 404.
The separate high-priority barrier/ammunition warning is appropriate and does not conflict with the general firing-range warning.
Gula Villan remains a valid conditional start landmark because SAT names it, but it was hardened as shared sat-uto lodging/start context and not a normal connector facility.
Gruvbryggan/Årsta, Ålö brygga, Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand records remain handoff-only context for sat-uto or sat-alo and should not render under the connector.
HiiKER and Komoot remain live but noisy, derivative or user-generated; neither should promote connector facilities or public drinking water.
Final JSON QA found no duplicate IDs or keys, no missing decision IDs, no guarded records in normal buckets, no unguarded metadata, no preview drift and no suspicious coordinate order issues.
remainingQuestions: Connector is complete for this research pass. During later app integration, keep the preview empty and preserve handoff records as non-rendering metadata unless an explicit cross-section UI is designed.

sections.name: Ålö
sections.routeShape: counterclockwise loop from Ålö brygga / Båtshaket, with optional handoff to Utö via Ålö Bridge
sourceHierarchyDraft: Current official SAT Ålö page, official step-by-step guide and 2025 SAT GPX.
Länsstyrelsen, Naturkartan, Skärgårdsstiftelsen/official reserve material and Båtshaket/operator pages for facilities, rules and access.
Waxholmsbolaget/SL current static and live timetables for access planning.
OSM/Wikimedia/Grillplatser/outdoor guide sources for coordinate corroboration and lower-risk detail.
AllTrails, HiiKER, Komoot, blogs and forums may support experience notes but should not override current official SAT facts or public-access caveats.

notes: Current SAT page and step guide say Ålö is a challenging 13.2 km section best hiked counterclockwise, with about 4.5 hours and 95 vertical metres.
Current 2025 GPX SAT Ålö H25 measures 13.225 km and supports the current 13.2 km value.
Older PDF/Outdooractive/OSM/Wikidata/Explore Archipelago values around 12.4 km should be preserved as stale-source conflict metadata.
Strong normal facility candidates after iteration 1 are Båtshaket seasonal restaurant, Ålö brygga four-way crossing water/toilet, Ålö Storsand water/toilet/barbecue cluster and Ålö Storsand beach.
Laxvik and Källviken barbecue areas were plausible after iteration 1 and were later promoted after iteration 2 rechecked coordinates and public/designated status.
Ålö Bridge pump remains suppressed as private/uncertain, and Rånö services must not leak into the Ålö section.
Iteration 2 promoted Laxvik and Källviken barbecue areas to normal fireplace/BBQ facilities after coordinate/on-route checks and corroboration from SAT plus map/community fire-place sources.
Iteration 2 kept Ålö brygga and Storsand water/toilet records as normal imports, with water phrased as signed/tagged drinking water plus island-service/seasonal verify-before-relying caveats.

Iteration 2 hardened Båtshaket as a normal seasonal restaurant with only 2025 operator hours found on 2026-04-27, added bike rental/return as optional logistics metadata, and suppressed customer-only toilets as public toilets.

Iteration 3 kept all normal water, toilet, restaurant and fireplace records stable, added display grouping guidance for Storsand/Laxvik/Källviken fireplaces, and promoted Laxvik beach as a normal POI.
Iteration 3 moved Tymarstugan from pending into guarded optional booked-lodging metadata: it exists and has a booking channel, but is not a public trail facility or public shelter.

Iteration 3 added guarded context-only viewpoints, wetland viewing-platform and waste-bin/disposal utility records, plus a suppression record preventing Ålö Storsand from being imported as a campsite.

Iteration 3 rechecked transport currentness: line 22 shoulder-period PDF is current for 2026 spring/autumn, s22 summer PDF remains stale 2025 material, and live planning is still required for exact travel dates.
Iteration 4 confirmed SAT EN/SV pages, step guide, GPX and KML remain current, while the 2024 print PDF remains stale/conflicting at 12.4 km.
Iteration 4 refined normal facility/POI coordinates from OSM/Naturkartan corroboration, kept all normal candidates, and added duplicate-handling guidance for Laxvik/Källviken/Storsand fire records.

Iteration 4 found Båtshaket still publishes only 2025 hours, line 22 shoulder timetable remains current, s22 and s40 summer PDFs remain stale 2025 material, and SL 43/43X is static-current only to 2026-06-18.
Iteration 4 kept Storsand campsite suppressed despite conflicting SAT news mentions, because municipal/local-order and reserve management evidence blocks normal campsite import until clarified.
Iteration 5 final sweep found no 2026 Båtshaket hours and no current 2026 summer line 22/Nordsyd static timetable, so the final Ålö import set remains unchanged from iteration 4.

Iteration 5 kept the Ålö wetland viewing platform as secondary nature context rather than a normal POI because official sources verify the feature but the exact platform point remains approximate/route-derived.

sections.descriptionDraft: A challenging, wild-feeling 13.2 km loop on Ålö, with technical coastal cliffs, forest paths, sandy beaches, pasture and gravel-road sections. The strongest public facilities are clustered at Ålö brygga/Båtshaket and Ålö Storsand; elsewhere hikers should be self-sufficient and respect Ålö-Rånö nature reserve rules.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Primary public access is Waxholmsbolaget line 22 from Nynäshamn via Nåttarö/Rånö to Ålö brygga, with exact travel-date planning in SL/Waxholmsbolaget. Ålö can also be reached on foot or by bike from Utö via the Utö-Ålö connector and Ålö Bridge. Båtshaket is the practical ferry-side service node in summer. Summer 2026 line-22/Nordsyd static times were not yet current in iteration 1; stale 2025 summer PDFs should not be used for 2026 departures.

gpxMetadata.outdooractiveAccessCaveat: Outdooractive page linked from SAT returned 403 in iteration 1; keep route id as provenance only.

measurement.decision: Use current official 13.2 km and 95 vertical metres for app-facing facts; raw point-to-point GPX gain/loss appears noisy and should not override official ascent.

kmlContext.measurement: KML longest coordinate block has 437 points and measures about 13.069 km; use as corroboration only.
kmlContext.parsingCaveat: Do not flatten the whole KML because it also contains a point marker.

stalePdfContext.handling: Older official print map/export. Preserve as conflict metadata; do not use over current SAT page/step guide/2025 GPX.

rulesDraft.name: Ålö-Rånö nature reserve rules
rulesDraft.description: Ålö is part of Ålö-Rånö nature reserve, protected since 2008 and managed by Skärgårdsstiftelsen. Dogs must be leashed, fires are allowed only at designated places, and camping/tenting more than two consecutive days is prohibited except at designated places. Do not damage geology, vegetation, trees or dead wood.

rulesDraft.name: Fire only at designated places
rulesDraft.description: Reserve rule: fires only at designated places. SAT adds that fires must respect fire bans and must not be lit on rocks. Current fire-ban state is dynamic.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress Ålö Storsand campsite marker
facilitiesToSuppressDraft.description: Do not import Ålö Storsand as a campsite. Ålö-Rånö management material also points to local restrictions against camping on bathing beaches. Keep Storsand as beach, water, toilet and barbecue context only until an official current clarification supports a campsite marker.

utilitiesDraft.name: Ålö brygga waste disposal context
utilitiesDraft.description: Mapped waste-disposal point near the Ålö brygga four-way service crossing, with Skärgårdsstiftelsen shown as operator in OSM. Keep optional/guarded only: SAT explicitly asks hikers to take generated garbage back to the mainland where waste management is available. Pack out all rubbish to the mainland; Ålö bins/waste points are limited island utilities and may be full, seasonal, removed or intended for local/day-use waste. Never leave bags or overflow beside bins.

utilitiesDraft.name: Ålö Storsand waste bins context
utilitiesDraft.description: Waste-bin context at Ålö Storsand. Naturkartan says bins are beside the bathing place and OSM maps a waste-basket node nearby. Keep optional/guarded and grouped with Storsand context only; pack-out remains the preferred route guidance. Pack out all rubbish to the mainland; Ålö bins/waste points are limited island utilities and may be full, seasonal, removed or intended for local/day-use waste. safetyWarningsDraft.name: Technical coastal and cliff terrain
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Official SAT marks Ålö as challenging. Several parts are technical coastal/cliff terrain, wet cliffs may be slippery, and the Ålö Bridge-to-ferry section includes steep/large rock steps.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Algal bloom bathing context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Ålö has several bathing places, especially Storsand, but Baltic algal blooms can make water unsafe, mainly July-September. Check current information near visit date.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Ticks and TBE context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Stockholm coastal and archipelago areas are TBE/tick-risk context. Check for ticks after hiking and use current 1177 guidance.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Utö firing-range approach handoff
safetyWarningsDraft.description: The Ålö section itself is not presented as a firing-range section, but hikers arriving from Utö cross the Utö-Ålö connector through/near Utö firing-range context. Keep as approach handoff only.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: Ålö emergency and sea rescue context
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: For emergencies call 112. For emergencies at sea, call 112 and ask for sea rescue, or use VHF channel 16 / Sweden Rescue if equipped. Ålö is ferry-dependent with limited immediate services.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: No verified AED on Ålö
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: Iteration 1 found no stable public source confirming an AED on Ålö or at Båtshaket. Do not show an AED marker unless verified in Hjärtstartarregistret or by an official local source.

Older official PDF, OSM/Wikidata and Explore Archipelago still show about 12.4 km and should be treated as stale/conflict metadata.
Strong normal facility candidates are Båtshaket seasonal restaurant, Ålö brygga four-way crossing water/toilet, Ålö Storsand water/toilet/barbecue cluster and Ålö Storsand beach.
Laxvik and Källviken barbecue areas are plausible but remain pending for another coordinate/designated-fireplace check.

Ålö-Rånö nature reserve rules require leashed dogs, fires only at designated places and no camping more than two consecutive nights except designated places.
No stable public AED on Ålö was confirmed; keep AED as unverified emergency metadata only.

sourceConflicts.summary: Current SAT EN/SV section pages and step guides list Rånö as 12 km. Current 2026 SAT print PDF, Outdooractive route and measured SAT GPX/KML geometry are about 12.3 km. Some third-party routes list about 10.8-10.9 km.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use 12.0 km for app-facing route facts; preserve 12.3 km and third-party values as geometry/export/conflict metadata.

sourceConflicts.summary: Current SAT EN/SV pages and step guides say Easy/Lätt and describe Rånö as non-technical. Current Outdooractive/PDF export labels the H25 export as difficult, while Komoot/AllTrails call it moderate.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use Easy because SAT's public section and guide text explicitly describe Rånö as easy; treat Outdooractive/PDF/third-party difficulty as conflict metadata.

sourceConflicts.summary: SAT step guides list 4.5 hours and 65 positive altitude metres. Outdooractive/PDF list 4:30, 60 m ascent and 55 m descent.
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use 4:30 and 65 m gain for app facts; store 60/55 m as print/Outdooractive geometry metadata.

sourceConflicts.preferredValue: guide-described counterclockwise route from and back to Rånö Källan / Rånö brygga

The official GPX/KML/Outdooractive geometry is ordered as a linear polyline starting at [58.938247, 18.213256] and ending at [58.933825, 18.178569].
sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Use the SAT guide narrative for start/end and direction. Use GPX/KML as authoritative geometry provenance, but do not treat first/last trackpoints as trailhead/end.

sourceConflicts.preferredTreatment: Suppress restaurant as normal 2026 food unless a newer operator source reverses the closure.

sections.descriptionDraft: An easy, mostly gravel-road Rånö section with open forest, beaches, swimming coves, designated campsite services and optional forest-path variants. The guide-described hike starts by the ferry/services at Rånö Källan, heads north through Rånö Gård and the northern out-and-back, then returns via Rånöhamn, Harviken/Skutviken and Rånö Källan.
sections.gettingThereDraft: Reach Rånö by Waxholmsbolaget ferry from Nynäshamn via Nåttarö/Aspö; boats continue toward Ålö before returning. SAT says Rånö can be reached from Nynäshamn, Ålö and Nåttarö year-round, and the North/South line follows the same route in summer. Use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning for exact dates.

measurement.decision: Use official SAT 12.0 km and 65 m gain for app facts; raw GPX gain/loss is noisy and the GPX ordering is not the guide start/end order.

kmlContext.parsingCaveat: Do not flatten the whole KML because it also contains a point marker.

printPdfContext.handling: Current but conflicting export. Preserve as metadata; do not override SAT page/guide route facts.

routeOrderRecommendation.reason: The official export behaves like an Outdooractive linearized lollipop/branch export with duplicate ferry spur context, not a clean closed loop in hiker guide order. A simple rotation at Rånö Källan would send the user west toward Knicksand first, while the SAT guide starts north.
routeOrderRecommendation.preferredImplementation: Keep the SAT GPX/KML as authoritative geometry provenance. If ordered turn-by-turn display is needed, build a derived guide-order geometry from the official geometry and guide narrative: Rånö Källan -> camping/Oxhagen -> Rånö Gård -> northern out-and-back/Gammelhamnsudd area -> Rånöhamn -> Harviken -> Skutviken -> Knicksand/Källan return, preserving branch semantics.

rulesDraft.name: Ålö-Rånö nature reserve rules
rulesDraft.description: Rånö is part of Ålö-Rånö nature reserve, protected since 2008 and managed by Skärgårdsstiftelsen. Dogs must be leashed, fires are allowed only at designated places, and tenting more than two consecutive days is prohibited except at designated places. Do not damage rock, soil, stone, vegetation, living or dead trees, or dead wood.

rulesDraft.name: Fire only at designated places
rulesDraft.description: Reserve rule: fires only at designated places. SAT also warns to respect fire bans and never light fires on rocks. Current fire-ban state is dynamic and must be checked near the visit date.

rulesDraft.name: Haninge local-order camping and dog context
rulesDraft.description: Haninge local-order rules currently treat Stockholm city bathing places on Gålö, Nåttarö, Rånö and Ålö, plus Stockholm city camping places on Gålö, Nåttarö and Rånö, as public-place-equivalent areas. Camping is prohibited on those areas except designated camping places, and dogs are barred from listed bathing-place areas from May 1 to September 30. This complements, not replaces, the nature-reserve leash and camping rules. Iteration 2 found no Rånö-specific proposed change in the May 1, 2026 revision context, but recheck Haninge's official författningssamling before final integration.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Algal bloom bathing context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Rånö has multiple swimming coves, cliffs and smaller sandy beaches, but Baltic algal blooms can make bathing unsafe, especially July-September. Keep children and dogs away from visible blooms and check current algal-bloom information near the visit date. Haninge's published routine test list does not include Rånö beaches, so do not imply regularly sampled municipal bathing-water status unless a current bath-water record is found.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Ticks and TBE context
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Stockholm coastal and archipelago areas are TBE/tick-risk context. Check for ticks after hiking and use current 1177 guidance; vaccination is recommended for people who live in or spend much time in risk areas.

safetyWarningsDraft.name: Limited island services and ferry dependence
safetyWarningsDraft.description: Rånö is ferry-dependent with limited services outside the main season. SAT says all services are about 100 m after the ferry quay, but the operator's 2026 page shows limited Rånö Livs spring hours and the summer restaurant closed for 2026. Carry water/food buffers and verify ferry/service hours before relying on the island.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: Rånö emergency and sea rescue context
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: For emergencies call 112. For emergencies at sea, call 112 and ask for sea rescue, or use VHF channel 16 / Sweden Rescue if equipped. Rånö Brygga practical information also tells visitors to state that they are on Rånö, with the cottage village at Knicksand, and to inform local staff when possible.

emergencyMetadataDraft.name: No verified AED on Rånö
emergencyMetadataDraft.description: Iteration 2 Hjärtstartarregistret map/WFS check found no verified AED/hjärtstartare on Rånö, at Rånö Livs, Rånö Brygga, the campground/Oxhagen or Rånökällan. Nearby hits were off-island on Norrö and Nåttarö/Aspö. Do not show an AED marker unless verified in Hjärtstartarregistret or by an official local/operator source.

integrationGuardrailsDraft: Coordinates are [lat, lon].
Use current SAT page/guide facts for distance/difficulty/time/ascent over current Outdooractive/PDF export conflicts.
Do not infer Rånö trailhead/end from the current GPX first/last trackpoints; use the guide-described Rånö Källan / Rånö brygga start/end.
Do not import Rånö Sommarkrog/Rånö Källan as active 2026 food unless a newer operator source reverses the closure.
Treat Rånö Livs as seasonal/limited-hours resupply, not year-round dependable food.
Keep Ålö and Nåttarö services out of Rånö normal imports.
Keep Skutviken water pending until current operator/official/field-photo confirmation; keep the northern-point fireplace coordinate suppressed as off-route/not verified designated.
Do not expose stugby guest showers, toilets, sauna, laundry or guest water as public trail facilities.
Fires only at designated places and only when fire bans allow.
Waste/recycling utilities should not encourage reliance on island bins; pack out rubbish when possible.
Keep SAT GPX/KML as official geometry provenance but do not blindly rotate it; for turn-by-turn UX, derive a guide-order geometry manually from official geometry and guide narrative.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial Rånö pass across official route facts/geometry, public facilities/services, access logistics, rules/safety/emergency and broad POI/source triangulation.
keyFindings: Current SAT page/guide facts support Rånö as Easy, 12 km, 4:30 and 65 positive altitude metres.
Current SAT GPX/KML/Outdooractive/PDF share route id 270406854 and measure about 12.3 km; the current print PDF is not stale but conflicts with SAT page/guide on distance and difficulty.
Official geometry is current but ordered as a linear Outdooractive export, so first/last trackpoints conflict with the guide-described Rånö Källan start/end.

Normal facility candidates after iteration 1 are Rånö Livs, Rånö Livs water, ferry-side public toilet, Rånö camping/water/toilet, Rånöhamn water/toilet, Skutviken toilet, Harviken fireplace and Knicksand BBQ cluster.
Normal POI candidates after iteration 1 are Knicksand beach, Harviken beach and Skutviken swimming cliffs.
Rånö Sommarkrog/Rånökällan should be suppressed as active 2026 food because the current operator page says the restaurant is closed for the 2026 season.
Rånö stugby belongs in optional booked-lodging metadata only; guest utilities must not render as public trail facilities.
Skutviken water and northern-point fireplace remain pending until later iterations verify current access/coordinates/designated status.
Line 22 spring/shoulder/autumn 2026 timetable is current; summer line 22/Nordsyd static PDFs remain stale 2025 material and require live planning.
Rånö is covered by Ålö-Rånö reserve rules: dogs leashed, fires only at designated places and no tenting more than two consecutive days except designated places.
No verified AED was found for Rånö in iteration 1.
Cross-section suppressions were added to keep Ålö and Nåttarö services out of Rånö normal imports.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 2 should verify exact public access and seasonality for Rånö Livs/brygga water, campsite water and Rånöhamn water from operator or field signage.
Iteration 2 should manually/map-side check Hjärtstartarregistret for any AED at Rånö Brygga or Rånö Livs.
Iteration 2 should resolve whether Skutviken pump is potable/current or should remain suppressed.
Iteration 2 should confirm whether Haninge local-order revision effective 2026-05-01 changes any Rånö beach/camping/dog treatment.
Iteration 2 should verify whether northern-point fireplace should move to normal import or stay pending.
Iteration 2 should decide whether to keep official GPX ordering as-is for geometry import or rotate/reorder the polyline around guide start/end.
Iteration 2 should review if Rånöhamn toilet/water and Skutviken toilet are sufficiently on-route and visitor-useful for normal markers or should be grouped/secondary.

iterationSummaries.focus: Second Rånö pass across water reliability, facility currentness, geometry ordering/proximity, rules/safety currentness and schema/import QA.
keyFindings: Rånö Livs has operator-published 2026 spring opening windows and should stay as a seasonal/limited-hours shop, not year-round resupply.
Rånö Sommarkrog remains suppressed as active 2026 food because the current operator page says the restaurant is closed for the 2026 season.
Campsite pump water is the strongest water record: operator says drinking water is controlled/safe and that the tent site has a manual pump.

Rånö Livs/brygga water and Rånöhamn water remain normal candidates with explicit seasonal/check-before-relying caveats; Skutviken water stays pending because primary confirmation is missing and SAT does not list it.
Stugby/reception utilities, showers, sauna, guest toilets, transport wagons and guest water remain optional/guest metadata or suppressions, not public trail facilities.
Use Rånö Källan/Rånö brygga for app-facing start/end metadata. Keep the current SAT GPX/KML as official geometry provenance but do not simply rotate it into guide order.
Route-proximity checks support Rånöhamn water/toilet, Skutviken toilet, camping/Oxhagen services, Knicksand beach/BBQ and Harviken fireplace as visitor-useful route-proximate records.
Northern-point fireplace remains pending: SAT names a fire pit, but the coordinate/currentness/designated status are not stable enough for normal import.
Kapelludden is about 1.3 km off the official route context and stays secondary/off-route.
Haninge rule revision context around 2026-05-01 did not reveal a Rånö-specific change in iteration 2, but the official författningssamling should still be rechecked before final integration.
No verified AED on Rånö was found in Hjärtstartarregistret; nearby AED hits are off-island on Norrö and Nåttarö/Aspö.
Schema/import QA found no duplicate Rånö IDs, no decision/preview drift, no guarded records in normal import arrays and valid [lat, lon] coordinates.
remainingQuestions: Iteration 3 should verify whether Rånö Livs/brygga water should stay as a normal seasonal marker or move to guarded-only if current public access cannot be confirmed beyond SAT/OSM/Wikimedia.
Iteration 3 should recheck whether the northern-point fireplace coordinate belongs on the Rånö route or is an OSM/source-placement artifact.
Iteration 3 should expand or normalize iteration summary source manifests if later tooling treats them as exhaustive.
Iteration 3 should look for any field reports/blogs/forums that confirm or contradict current Rånöhamn, Skutviken and Knicksand utility access after 2025 field checks.

iterationSummaries.focus: Third Rånö pass across contested water records, northern-fireplace status, community/field triangulation, source-manifest/import-shape QA and access/service currentness.
keyFindings: Rånö Livs/brygga water remains a normal seasonal water marker: SAT names water by the shop, OSM history supports drinking_water/seasonal context and 2025 Wikimedia field photos support the point, but wording must remain check-before-relying.
Rånöhamn water remains a normal seasonal water marker: SAT names it, and OSM/Wikimedia evidence shows April 2025 off-season and August 2025 summer-on states.
Skutviken water remains pending only: SAT does not list it, OSM/note evidence is uncertain about whether the pump works, and nearby toilet tagging says drinking_water=no.

The northern/Gammelhamnsudd fireplace coordinate is suppressed rather than pending: the OSM point is about 725 m off the SAT route and is not listed in Skärgårdsstiftelsen/Explore Archipelago grillplats service data.

Field/community triangulation confirms Knicksand/Stugbyn as a west-side beach/stugby/BBQ context, Harviken as beach plus grill/firepit, Rånöhamn as natural harbor with water, and Skutviken as natural harbor/toilet context with uncertain water.

Rånö camping/Oxhagen remains the reliable designated campsite with pump/toilet context, but an August 2025 OSM note asks whether the toilet still exists, so later passes should recheck toilet currentness.
Line 22 spring/shoulder/autumn 2026 remains current; summer line 22/Nordsyd static PDFs are still 2025-stale and should remain live-planner-only.
BOUT stays private fallback metadata, and bike/kayak rental stays SAT-only unverified activity context because current Rånö operator pages do not confirm rental inventory/hours/prices.
Iteration summary sourceUrls are research highlights, not exhaustive manifests; record-level sources remain the authoritative source set unless later tooling normalizes all URLs.

iterationSummaries.focus: Fourth Rånö pass across campsite toilet currentness, 2026 ferry/timetable state, bike/kayak rental verification, source-manifest schema QA and contradiction sweep.
keyFindings: Rånö camping/Oxhagen toilet stays as a normal marker but with guarded-currentness notes: April 2025 photo/newer OSM node/operator/campsite evidence support it, while an unresolved August 2025 OSM note asks whether an older mapped toilet remains.
Rånö Livs/brygga water stays normal seasonal but needs a stronger outage caveat because a 2025-08-02 field photo documents temporary closure due water shortage.
Skutviken toilet remains normal and Skutviken water remains pending/suppressed; OSM note evidence only says a pump should exist up in the forest, not that it is current, potable or public.

Current 2026 summer static line 22/Nordsyd PDFs have not replaced stale 2025 files; keep summer departures live-planner-only until current PDFs or planner evidence exists.

Normal/preview ID alignment remains clean; bathing preview records are mapped to supported TrailFacility type swimming and no guarded records leak into appImportPreviewDraft.

iterationSummaries.focus: Final Rånö audit across Rånöhamn toilet confidence, volatile current sources, import decision arrays, source quality/readiness and missing source classes.
keyFindings: Rånö is ready for manual app import with guardrails: import 11 normal facilities and 3 normal POIs from appImportPreviewDraft.

Final volatile-source check found no changes since iteration 4: Rånö Sommarkrog remains closed for 2026, Rånö Livs remains limited-hours seasonal, Rånö Livs water needs outage caveats, campsite toilet currentness watch remains, and summer ferry PDFs remain 2025-stale.

No guarded, suppressed, guest-only or metadata-only records leak into normal facility, normal POI or preview arrays.

sections.name: Nåttarö
sections.routeShape: near_loop_from_nattaro_ferry_quay_and_affarsbacken
sections.descriptionDraft: A compact but demanding Nåttarö loop from the ferry-side service cluster, mixing easy gravel road through the holiday-village area with technical east-coast walking over rocks, roots, shingle beaches and sandy coves. The strongest visitor themes are Storsand and Skarsand, Östermarsfladen/Östermarviken, Vänsviken, the snorkel trail, Drottninggrottan and the island's reserve rules.

sourceConflicts: SAT web/step-guide facts say 9.5 km, challenging, 4.5 hours and 55 positive altitude meters.
The current 2025-10 H25 Outdooractive PDF says about 9.3 km, moderate, 2:20 and 38 m ascent/descent.
An older 2024 official PDF still indexed online says 8.7 km, difficult and 4:00; treat as superseded conflict evidence, not canonical.
Komoot/OSM/Nåttarö operator and AllTrails variants describe shorter or differently-measured routes; do not use them as canonical SAT length.
namedRouteSequenceDraft: Expedition, restaurant, beach and service cluster
Three-way intersection by the grocery store
Return toward Affärsbacken and ferry-side services

appGeometryHandlingDraft.crossSectionLeakage: Access text mentions Rånö, Ålö, Utö and Landsort, but H25 geometry bounds stay on Nåttarö.
appGeometryHandlingDraft.routeProximityHandling: Use a buffered route corridor for app import rather than strict raw GPX bbox rejection. Two normal preview records sit just outside the raw H25 bbox but are legitimate route/service-cluster records: Nåttarö camping is about 45-50 m west of bbox minLon and Östermarviken fire pits are about 7 m north of bbox maxLat.

facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal grocery store near the ferry-side service cluster, selling food, camping supplies and practical island items. Iteration 4 treats the operator's 2026 page as current and the OSM opening_hours=closed value as stale 2025 metadata; display as seasonal/check-current-hours resupply, not year-round dependable resupply.

facilitiesDraft.name: Östermarkiosken
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: 2026 seasonal opening listed as 2026-06-26 at 11:00; weather-dependent opening caveat
facilitiesDraft.description: Small seasonal kiosk by Östermarsfladen/Östermar with ice cream, coffee, drinks, snacks and beach items. Iteration 3 moved this to the mapped kiosk-building coordinate; it may also handle bread preorders from Handelsboden.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö Krog
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: seasonal; operator says the restaurant opens at Valborg, runs weekends until Midsummer, has exact 2026 times pending and includes closure for staff care on 2026-09-06
facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal restaurant near the ferry/service cluster. Operator sources should override OSM reservation snippets: normal table booking is not offered, while larger group menus may be prebooked. Use check-current-hours wording until the operator publishes exact 2026 daily times.

facilitiesDraft.name: Sixtens Bodega
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: seasonal; current operator page says closed until Midsummer 2026 and opens at Midsummer
facilitiesDraft.description: Seasonal pizza, ice-cream and takeaway/cafe point beside the service house. Keep as secondary-priority food because it is real and public when open, but customer toilets must not become public trail toilets. Ignore stale third-party/OSM closure snippets when they conflict with the current operator page.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö camping
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: operator says 2026 lodging/camping booking is open; Swedish practical-info page says open Valborg to last weekend in September and closed on Midsummer Eve
facilitiesDraft.description: Designated 24-hour camping near the central service cluster. Iteration 4 operator rules: open from Valborg to the last weekend in September, closed on Midsummer Eve, maximum seven nights, 18+ without guardian, two dry toilets at the tent area, water in the dish room, a grill place near the tent area and 2026 tent fees of 60 SEK per tent/night or 120 SEK for larger tents. Reserve rules still apply outside the designated campsite; prefer the Swedish operator practical-info page over stale translated lodging pages.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö ferry quay public dry toilet
facilitiesDraft.description: Accessible public dry toilet near the ferry quay/service cluster. Länsstyrelsen lists an adapted dry toilet near the ferry pier and OSM tags the mapped toilet as official and 24/7.

facilitiesDraft.name: Östermarsfladen dry toilets
facilitiesDraft.description: Dry toilets at Östermarsfladen/Östermar. Supported by Länsstyrelsen and OSM; treat the paired mapped toilets as a single service cluster.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö Storsand dry toilet

currentness.issue: Länsstyrelsen, Naturkartan and OSM/photo evidence support the Storsand toilet, but the current OSM check_date value is malformed as 2025-06-31.
currentness.handling: Keep as normal because the facility is corroborated; treat the malformed OSM date as metadata noise and use 2025 photo/edit history for currentness.

facilitiesDraft.description: Dry toilet serving Storsand/Stora Sand. Iteration 2 confirms it is route-relevant and importable; keep a source-currentness caveat because the OSM node has malformed check_date metadata.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö west/harbor service-cluster drinking water
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: seasonal summer tap; verify before relying
facilitiesDraft.description: Normal public water marker for the west/harbor service cluster by the ferry quay/guest harbor, anchored on the signed Dricksvatten tap. Iteration 5 found additional OSM drinking-water=yes taps around the west/camping/lodging service area, but keeps them as cluster evidence rather than separate normal pins.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö camping/service-area water context
facilitiesDraft.seasonality: seasonal/service-area-dependent; verify before relying
facilitiesDraft.description: Water in the camping/service-area context near the route. Iteration 4 demotes this from normal public trail water: the operator says campers fetch water in the dish room, Naturkartan frames it as campsite water, and OSM/photo evidence is tied to a toilet/washbasin/service node rather than a standalone public trail tap.

facilitiesDraft.name: Nåttarö harbor rentals
facilitiesDraft.description: Confirmed operator rental cluster for kayaks, bicycles, rowing boats and SUPs at/near the harbor office. This supports on-island activity and short links, not scheduled access to the island.

facilitiesDraft.name: Östermarviken fire pits
facilitiesDraft.description: Clustered designated fire-pit area around Östermarviken/Östermarsfladen. Iteration 2 moves the marker to the west/southwest shore cluster rather than the broader bay coordinate; use only when fire bans allow and never directly on rocks.

facilitiesDraft.name: Skarsand fire pits
facilitiesDraft.description: Clustered designated fire-pit context at/near Skarsand. Iteration 2 separates this from the beach marker and uses the photo-backed OSM/Grillplatser cluster.

facilitiesDraft.name: Storsand fire pit
facilitiesDraft.description: Clustered designated fire/grill context at Storsand/Stora Sand, using a route-proximate 2025 photo-backed OSM/Grillplatser marker. Fire bans override.

facilitiesDraft.name: Vänsviken fire pit
facilitiesDraft.description: Designated fire/grill context at Vänsviken, the southern/eastern bay rest area named by SAT and community route guides, using the photo-backed Grillplatser/OSM marker.

pendingFacilityDraft.name: Östermar / Östermarsfladen water
pendingFacilityDraft.description: SAT lists water at Östermarviken, but iteration 2 confirmed the mapped tap exists with drinking_water=no after a 2025-07-31 check and a sign warning that water shortage/discoloration makes it suitable for washing/dishes but not drinking. Keep pending/non-potable until new operator or field confirmation reverses this.

pendingFacilityDraft.description: Real public firepit near Kvarnviken/Ångbåtsbryggan with 2025 photo/Grillplatser evidence, but SAT's official cooking-fire list names Östermarviken, Skarsand, Storsand and Vänsviken. Keep as optional service-cluster context, not a fifth normal SAT fireplace.

pendingFacilityDraft.name: Nåttarö tent-area grill
pendingFacilityDraft.description: Confirmed grill by the tent area; useful campsite metadata but not a separate normal SAT fire marker because the campsite record already carries this context.

pendingFacilityDraft.description: Bins are documented around camping and selected visitor areas, but no robust recycling-station record was verified. Keep as utility text: limited bins exist, and visitors should carry waste out when practical.

facilitiesToSuppressDraft.name: Suppress southern Nåttarö Hals toilet for SAT import

rulesDraft.protectedArea: Nåttarö nature reserve; includes Natura 2000 SE0110201 Södra Nåttarö.
rulesDraft.dogs: Dogs must be leashed in the reserve; Länsstyrelsen rule is stricter/all-year than SAT's March-September text.
rulesDraft.fires: Fires only at designated places; fire bans override; do not light fires on rocks.
rulesDraft.camping: Camping may not exceed two consecutive days except at designated places; operator campsite terms allow longer paid campsite stays up to local maximum.
rulesDraft.birdProtection: Access bans apply in Nåttaröfladen bird-protection areas from 1 Feb to 15 Aug and for Bodskär/Österskär from 1 Apr to 31 Jul.
otherRestrictions: Do not damage rock, soil, stones, vegetation, living/dead trees or bushes.
Aircraft takeoff/landing is prohibited except designated/official exceptions.

safetyWarningsDraft.message: The east coast section is technical with narrow trail, rocks, roots, cliff passages, sparse marking in places and slippery conditions when wet.
The pine-covered island has no local firefighting service; use only designated fire pits and check current fire bans.
Nåttarö has no road exit; exact boat departures, weather disruptions and seasonal timetable gaps must be checked before travel.

waterReliabilityDraft.summary: Iteration 5 keeps one west/harbor service-cluster drinking-water marker as normal public trail water, anchored on the signed ferry quay/guest-harbor tap. Additional OSM drinking_water=yes nodes around the west/camping/lodging service area are cluster evidence, not separate normal pins. Camping/service-area water is real campsite/service metadata but demoted from normal public trail water; Östermar is confirmed non-potable/pending after a 2025 warning sign, and Storsand is pending because no exact public potable tap was verified despite SAT text.
waterReliabilityDraft.seasonalityCaveat: Treat all island water as seasonal/service-dependent and advise carrying water from start.

Iteration 1 used some beach/bay coordinates for fire contexts. Iteration 2 moved Östermar, Skarsand, Storsand and Vänsviken to route-proximate OSM/Grillplatser/photo-backed clusters.
OSM reservation snippets reportedly conflict with operator no-normal-table-booking wording.
Reserve camping limit is two consecutive days except designated places; operator campsite allows paid stays up to seven nights.

Line 22 shoulder/autumn PDF is current. Iteration 4 found direct s22/s29/s40/s852 URLs, but their extracted validity text is still 2025; use them only as stale-conflict evidence until official 2026 summer rows/times appear.

appImportDecisionDraft.iteration5Caveat: Final Nåttarö import keeps 14 normal facilities and 4 normal POIs. Sixtens Bodega remains normal seasonal food, and the camping/service-area water remains metadata-only. The west/harbor water record is a single cluster marker, not a claim that only one public tap exists around the service area. Extra ferry-side firepit, tent-area grill, camping/service toilets, waste bins and cultural/nature POIs remain secondary/enrichment only; Östermar and Storsand water remain pending, and direct summer timetable PDFs found in iterations 4-5 still contain 2025 validity text.

iterationSummaries.focus: Initial five-way Nåttarö research across official route facts, public facilities, transport, rules/safety and broad third-party POI triangulation.
keyFindings: Use SAT web/step-guide facts for user-facing metadata: Nåttarö, 9.5 km, challenging, 4.5 hours, 55 positive meters and clockwise direction.
Use the official H25 GPX/Outdooractive export as geometry source; it is a near-loop with about 599 points and calculated GPX length about 9.289 km.
Core public seasonal services cluster around the ferry quay/Affärsbacken: Handelsboden, Bryggkiosken, Nåttarö Krog, camping, public toilet, visitor water and rental office.
East-coast visitor/service context includes Östermarsfladen/Östermarviken, Skarsand, Storsand and Vänsviken; exact water and fire-pit coordinates need deeper route-proximity QA in later iterations.
Nåttarö Handelsbod current 2026 page says the shop is running again; Bryggkiosken opens 2026-06-19 and Östermarkiosken has a preliminary 2026-06-26 opening.
Nåttarö camping is a real paid designated campsite, while stugby, hostel, shower, sauna and most lodging utilities should stay guest/booked metadata rather than free public trail facilities.
SAT lists open toilets and water at ferry quay, Östermarviken and Nåttarö Storsand, but Östermar water is pending because an OSM/field-note context warns against drinking from one nearby tap.
Waxholmsbolaget line 22 is the primary access from Nynäshamn; current static PDFs cover spring/shoulder/autumn 2026 but not the summer 2026 gap.
Nordsyd has a stated 2026 date range on SAT but detailed line 40/static times found in iteration 1 are still 2025, so exact summer times must remain live-planner-only.
Nåttarö is a nature reserve with all-year dog leash rule, designated-fire-only rule, camping limits except designated places, bird-protection closures and Natura 2000 context.
High-value enrichment POIs are Storsand, Skarsand, the snorkel trail, Drottninggrottan, Östermarsfladen/Ryssugnar, Vänsviken and secondary Nåttaröhals/Halsudden context.
No official bathing-water quality status was found for Nåttarö beaches in Haninge/HaV lists; do not import quality ratings.
